# Introduction

GenicUI is an **MCP-native, generative agentic UI framework** rendered as Web Components. It lets any AI agent — Claude Code, GPT, Cursor, or your own — render, update, and respond to real UI components in your existing application.

You keep your component library (PrimeVue, Mantine, shadcn, Skeleton, anything). GenicUI wraps it with a thin adapter, declares each component's contract in one place, and exposes the catalog through four standard MCP tools.

## Why GenicUI?

Most AI-agent UI integrations fall into one of three traps. GenicUI avoids all of them.

### MCP-native, not framework-only

GenicUI speaks the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} directly. Any MCP-capable agent discovers your components via `find_ui_component`, mounts them via `render_component`, updates them via `update_component`, and subscribes to user interactions via `subscribe_to_events`. There is no proprietary SDK for the agent to install.

::callout{type="info"}
The four MCP tools are the entire wire protocol. If your agent supports MCP, it supports GenicUI.
::

### Web Components, not iframes

Components render as native `<genic-element>` custom elements inside your application's DOM tree. They inherit your CSS variables, your theme, your layout system, and your accessibility context. No sandboxed iframe. No postMessage plumbing. No styling collisions.

### JSON-Patch wire, not full re-render

When the agent updates a component, GenicUI ships a [RFC 6902 JSON-Patch](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6902){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} over the wire — only the changed properties traverse the network. The browser applies the patch to the live component instance. Render cost stays O(diff) instead of O(component).

## How it fits

```text
┌──────────┐    MCP tools     ┌──────────────┐   WebSocket   ┌──────────────┐
│  Agent   │ ───────────────► │ GenicUI      │ ─────────────►│   Browser    │
│ (Claude) │   JSON-RPC POST  │ server       │  JSON-Patch   │  <genic-     │
│  Code)   │ ◄─────────────── │ (port 3040)  │ ◄───────────── │   element>   │
└──────────┘                  └──────────────┘               └──────────────┘
                                     │
                                     ▼
                              ┌──────────────┐
                              │   Registry   │
                              │  (catalog +  │
                              │  schemas)    │
                              └──────────────┘
```

1. **Agent** discovers the `DataTable` component by calling `find_ui_component({ tag: "table" })`.
2. **Server** resolves the catalog entry, validates props against the TypeBox schema, and mounts the component.
3. **Browser** receives the mount frame over WebSocket and renders `<genic-element>` inside your app.
4. **User** clicks a row → the event is forwarded back to the server → the agent's next turn sees `row_selected` as a tool result.

## Who it's for

| Role                         | Use GenicUI for                                                                                   |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Agent developers**         | Shipping a chat surface where the model calls real UI instead of returning JSON blobs.            |
| **Framework shim consumers** | Wrapping PrimeVue / Mantine / shadcn so an external agent can drive them without a custom SDK.    |
| **Registry authors**         | Publishing a typed component catalog that any MCP-capable agent can consume.                      |
| **Operators**                | Running GenicUI in a multi-tenant environment with per-tenant API keys and component allow-lists. |

## What you get

- **Five core packages** — `@genicui/core`, `@genicui/server`, `@genicui/client`, `@genicui/vite-plugin`, `@genicui/agent-bridge`.
- **One reference registry** — `@genicul-primevue/registry` with six production-ready components.
- **A live playground** — `examples/playground/` boots a Nuxt 4 app wired to a real GenicUI server.
- **A working Claude Code integration** — register the server via `claude mcp add` and start rendering components from chat.

# Installation

Install GenicUI's three runtime packages in any project that speaks WebSocket. The full reference walkthrough below targets **Nuxt 4** — the most-tested integration — but the server is framework-agnostic and runs anywhere Bun or Node runs.

## Prerequisites

::tabs
  :::tab{label="Bun (preferred)"}
  Bun 1.3.12 or later. GenicUI's server uses Bun's native WebSocket and HTTP server. [Install Bun](https://bun.sh/docs/installation){rel=""nofollow""}.

  ```bash
  bun --version
  # >= 1.3.12
  ```
  :::

  :::tab{label="Node.js"}
  Node.js 20 LTS or later. The server runs on Node via Elysia's Node adapter with equivalent behavior.

  ```bash
  node --version
  # >= v20.0.0
  ```
  :::
::

You also need:

- A package manager — `bun`, `npm`, `pnpm`, or `yarn`.
- A working Nuxt 4 project (or any Vite-based app) for the client side.

## Scaffold a new project

::steps
### Create a fresh Nuxt 4 app

```bash
bun create nuxt@latest my-genicui-app
cd my-genicui-app
```

When the CLI prompts you to pick modules, skip `@nuxt/ui` for now — GenicUI ships its own components and you do not need a UI framework to render them.

### Install the GenicUI runtime

```bash
bun add @genicui/core @genicui/server @genicui/client
```

- **`@genicui/core`** — shared types, JSON-Patch engine, session store. Zero runtime dependencies.
- **`@genicui/server`** — Elysia HTTP + WebSocket server, MCP transport, four MCP tools.
- **`@genicui/client`** — `<genic-element>` Web Component, WebSocket client, React/Vue adapters.

### (Optional) Install the build + LLM adapters

```bash
bun add -D @genicui/vite-plugin
bun add @genicui/agent-bridge
```

- **`@genicui/vite-plugin`** — AST scans your Vue/React/Svelte sources for component schemas and emits `genui-registry.json` at build time.
- **`@genicui/agent-bridge`** — fetch-based LLM + MCP client you can drop into a Node backend to drive a GenicUI server from any model.

### (Optional) Install a component registry

```bash
bun add @genicul-primevue/registry
```

The PrimeVue registry ships six production components — `DataTable`, `Calculator`, `WeatherCard`, `CityPicker`, and more — each declared once in `registry.json` and rendered as Web Components in any framework.
::

## Configure your project

### 1. Start the GenicUI server

Create `server/genicui.ts` at the repo root:

```ts [server/genicui.ts]
import { createServer } from '@genicui/server';

createServer();
```

Then add a script to `package.json`:

```json [package.json]
{
  "scripts": {
    "genicui": "bun run server/genicui.ts"
  }
}
```

The server listens on `http://localhost:3040` by default. Override with `GENICUI_PORT` and `GENICUI_HOSTNAME` environment variables.

::callout{type="info"}
`createServer()`

 reads 

`GENICUI_API_KEY`

 and 

`GENICUI_REGISTRIES_DIR`

 from the environment. In dev mode, leaving 

`GENICUI_API_KEY`

 unset disables auth — every request is accepted. See 

[Trust Boundary](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/trust-boundary)

 for production setup.
::

### 2. Mount the client in your app

For Nuxt 4, create a plugin:

```ts [app/plugins/genicui.client.ts]
import { defineNuxtPlugin } from '#app';
import { connectGenicUiClient } from '@genicui/client';

export default defineNuxtPlugin((nuxtApp) => {
  const client = connectGenicUiClient({
    url: 'ws://localhost:3040/ws',
  });
  nuxtApp.vueApp.provide('genicui', client);
});
```

For React, SvelteKit, or vanilla HTML, see the framework-specific recipes in [Guides → Development](https://genicui.vaah.ai/guides/development).

### 3. Render your first component

Add `<genic-element>` to any template:

```vue [app/pages/index.vue]
<template>
  <genic-element component-id="my-table" />
</template>
```

The server assigns the component ID when you call `render_component`. To trigger a render from your own code, POST to the MCP endpoint:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3040/mcp \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "jsonrpc": "2.0",
    "id": 1,
    "method": "tools/call",
    "params": {
      "name": "render_component",
      "arguments": {
        "name": "DataTable",
        "props": { "rows": [] }
      }
    }
  }'
```

The response includes the assigned `componentId`. Pass that to `<genic-element>` and the table renders.

## Verify the install

::steps
### Start the server

```bash
bun run genicui
# → Server running at http://0.0.0.0:3040
```

### Hit the health endpoint

```bash
curl http://localhost:3040/health
# → {"status":"ok"}
```

### Open the playground

```bash
git clone https://github.com/vaah-ai/GenicUI.git
cd GenicUI/examples/playground
bun install
bun run dev
# → http://localhost:3000
```

The playground bundles a chat surface wired to the GenicUI server. Type "render a data table" and the agent renders one inline.
::

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom                              | Likely cause                          | Fix                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `EADDRINUSE :::3040`                 | Another process holds port 3040       | Set `GENICUI_PORT=4040` and update the client's `ws://...` URL            |
| `WebSocket connection failed`        | Server is on a different port/host    | Check `GENICUI_PORT` and the client's `url` field                         |
| `Component "X" not found in catalog` | Registry directory not loaded         | Set `GENICUI_REGISTRIES_DIR=./registries` and verify the directory exists |
| `<genic-element>` renders nothing    | Component never mounted on the server | Confirm `render_component` was called and the `componentId` matches       |

# Quick Start

This walkthrough renders a real `DataTable` component from a Claude Code agent, then captures a `row_selected` event back into the model. Total elapsed time: **under five minutes** on a fresh checkout with Bun installed.

::callout{type="info"}
**Prerequisites:**

 Bun 1.3.12+, a Claude Code install with the MCP CLI, and 

`git`

. The example uses the bundled PrimeVue registry so you do not need any other UI framework.
::

## The five-minute flow

::steps
### Start the GenicUI server

```bash
git clone https://github.com/vaah-ai/GenicUI.git
cd GenicUI
bun install
bun --filter @genicui/server start
# → Server running at http://0.0.0.0:3040
```

The server boots on port `3040` and auto-loads every registry under `registries/`. The PrimeVue registry ships with the repo, so `DataTable` is available immediately.

Verify the server is healthy:

```bash
curl http://localhost:3040/health
# → {"status":"ok"}
```

### Register the server with Claude Code

Add the GenicUI server as an MCP endpoint. Claude Code discovers the four tools (`find_ui_component`, `render_component`, `update_component`, `subscribe_to_events`) and exposes them to the model.

```bash
claude mcp add genicui \
  --transport http \
  --url http://localhost:3040/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer dev"
```

  :::callout{type="warning"}
  `Authorization: Bearer dev`

   is a dev-mode placeholder. In production, set 

  `GENICUI_API_KEY`

   on the server and pass 

  `Bearer gnc_live_<32-char-key>`

   from the client. See 

  [Trust Boundary](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/trust-boundary)

   for production setup.
  :::

Confirm the registration:

```bash
claude mcp list
# → genicui: http://localhost:3040/mcp (connected)
```

### Open the playground chat surface

The playground at `examples/playground/` is a Nuxt 4 app with a chat panel wired to the same WebSocket.

```bash
bun --filter genicui-playground dev
# → http://localhost:3000
```

Open the URL in your browser. You should see a three-zone layout: registry sidebar, prompt chips, and a chat panel.

### Render a DataTable from a chat prompt

In the playground chat, type:

```text
Render a data table with three rows.
```

The Claude Code agent calls `find_ui_component({ name: "DataTable" })`, then `render_component({ name: "DataTable", props: { rows: [...] } })`. The chat bubble embeds the rendered `<DataTable>` PrimeVue component inline — sortable, paginated, and styled by the playground's theme.

### Click a row → receive the event

Click any row in the rendered table. The browser fires a `row_selected` event back to the GenicUI server, which forwards it to Claude Code as a synthetic tool result. The model's next turn sees:

```json
{
  "action": "row_selected",
  "detail": { "rowId": "row-2" }
}
```

You can verify the event was captured by typing "what row did I just click?" — the agent responds with the row's data.
::

## What just happened

| Step     | MCP tool                                                         | Result                                   |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| Discover | `find_ui_component({ name: "DataTable" })`                       | Catalog hit — returns schema + events    |
| Mount    | `render_component({ name, props, idempotencyKey })`              | Component mounts, `componentId` returned |
| Wire     | `subscribe_to_events({ componentId, events: ["row_selected"] })` | Server starts forwarding events          |
| Update   | (later) `update_component({ componentId, patch })`               | JSON-Patch applied to live instance      |
| Capture  | (browser → server)                                               | Event frame relayed to agent             |

## Verify it worked

If the table did not render, walk down this checklist:

1. **Server is up?** `curl http://localhost:3040/health` returns `{"status":"ok"}`.
2. **MCP is connected?** `claude mcp list` shows `genicui: connected`.
3. **Registry loaded?** `curl http://localhost:3040/api/registries` lists the PrimeVue registry (requires `Authorization` header in production).
4. **Component exists?** From Claude Code, ask "what components are available?" — the agent lists them via `find_ui_component`.
5. **No CORS error?** Open the browser devtools network tab; the WebSocket upgrade at `/ws` should be `101 Switching Protocols`.

::callout{type="error"}
**Symptom:**

 

`Component "DataTable" not found in catalog`

.


**Cause:**

 The registry directory is not on the server's load path.


**Fix:**

 

`GENICUI_REGISTRIES_DIR=./registries bun --filter @genicui/server start`

 from the repo root.
::

## Going further

You now have a working end-to-end GenicUI pipeline. To extend it:

- **Wrap your own components** — see [Guides → Authoring a Custom Registry](https://genicui.vaah.ai/guides/custom-registry).
- **Drive the server from your own backend** — see [`@genicui/agent-bridge`](https://genicui.vaah.ai/api/agent-bridge).
- **Deploy to Cloudflare Workers** — see [Deployment → Cloudflare](https://genicui.vaah.ai/deployment/cloudflare).
- **Ship a production-hardened server with API keys** — see [Concepts → Trust Boundary](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/trust-boundary).

# Protocol

GenicUI carries every interaction as a single-line JSON frame on a WebSocket. Four fields are mandatory (`v`, `channel`, `type`, `payload`) plus a monotonic `seq` counter; reserved channels and AG-UI event names define what the frame *means*. This page is the wire-level reference — the canonical shapes for everything GenicUI emits and accepts.

## What the wire frame looks like

```text
┌──────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ v            │ Protocol version. Always "1". Frames with v != 1 → 1003. │
├──────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ channel      │ String, 1-128 chars, no control chars.                   │
│              │  • "__session__" reserved (server.hello, session.*)      │
│              │  • "__mcp__" reserved (TOOL_CALL_*, errors)              │
│              │  • "__agent__" reserved (agent responses)                │
│              │  • "<componentId>" for one mounted component             │
├──────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ type         │ AG-UI event name (e.g. STATE_DELTA) or GenicUI-specific. │
│              │ Server validates against known event list.               │
├──────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ payload      │ Schema-conformant JSON object. Shape depends on type.    │
├──────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ seq          │ uint64 monotonic per channel. Out-of-order frames buffer. │
└──────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

A complete frame on the wire:

```text
{"v":1,"channel":"dt-sess9f8e-01HK9X","type":"STATE_DELTA","payload":[{"op":"replace","path":"/rows/1/name","value":"updated"}],"seq":42}
```

`Source: packages/core/src/sequence.ts:42` for the canonical `envelope()` helper that builds this shape.

## Why a flat envelope

The envelope stays flat — no nested envelope header — for three reasons:

1. **JSON-line framing.** Every frame is one line of UTF-8 JSON, terminated by `\n`. Line-buffered parsers in Caddy, Cloudflare Workers, and Bun all handle this without a custom decoder.
2. **One channel per frame.** `channel` is a first-class key, so a multiplexer can route a frame to the right subscriber in O(1).
3. **`seq` at the top level.** Reordering and dedupe happen at the channel layer, not deep inside payload schemas.

::callout{type="info"}
The wire frame is also the unit of replay. F33 (Session Recovery) buffers the last 500 frames per channel and replays them by 

`Last-Event-ID`

 on reconnect.
::

## The 14 AG-UI events

GenicUI emits a subset of the AG-UI event taxonomy alongside GenicUI-specific events. The 14 events below are the entire surface — there is no other type that crosses the wire.

| #  | Event                  | Emitted by    | Payload shape                               | When                                                     |
| -- | ---------------------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1  | `RUN_STARTED`          | server        | `{ runId }`                                 | First event in an agent turn.                            |
| 2  | `RUN_FINISHED`         | server        | `{ runId }`                                 | Last event in an agent turn.                             |
| 3  | `TOOL_CALL_STARTED`    | server        | `{ toolCallId, toolName }`                  | Begins a tool invocation.                                |
| 4  | `TOOL_CALL_ARGS`       | server        | `{ toolCallId, args }`                      | Carries the tool's JSON arguments.                       |
| 5  | `TOOL_CALL_RESULT`     | server        | `{ toolCallId, result, isError? }`          | Completes the tool invocation.                           |
| 6  | `STATE_SNAPSHOT`       | server        | `{ componentId, state }`                    | Full state — initial mount or patch fallback.            |
| 7  | `STATE_DELTA`          | server        | `{ componentId, patch: JsonPatchOp[] }`     | Incremental update via RFC 6902.                         |
| 8  | `COMPONENT_MOUNTED`    | server        | `{ componentId, schema, initialState }`     | New component goes live. Precedes any `STATE_DELTA`.     |
| 9  | `COMPONENT_UNMOUNTED`  | server        | `{ componentId }`                           | Component tears down.                                    |
| 10 | `COMPONENT_EVENT`      | client→server | `{ componentId, action, detail }`           | User-driven action from a mounted component.             |
| 11 | `subscription.created` | server        | `{ subscriptionId, componentId, events }`   | Filter subscription is live.                             |
| 12 | `subscription.closed`  | server        | `{ subscriptionId, reason }`                | Filter subscription ended (unmount, unsubscribe, error). |
| 13 | `channel.closed`       | server        | `{ componentId, reason }`                   | Channel torn down — listeners must drop state.           |
| 14 | `server.hello`         | server        | `{ sessionId, serverVersion, heartbeatMs }` | First frame after WS upgrade. Channel `__session__`.     |

::callout{type="warning"}
Server rejects any 

`type`

 not in this list with WS code 1003 (unsupported data). Adding a new event type requires updating both the server validator and every client subscriber — keep the list closed.
::

## JSON-RPC framing for tool calls

Tool calls use a thin JSON-RPC 2.0 envelope. The four MCP tools (`find_ui_component`, `render_component`, `update_component`, `subscribe_to_events`) all travel as JSON-RPC requests on the `__mcp__` channel.

::code-group
```json [Request]
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": "tc-1",
  "method": "render_component",
  "params": {
    "name": "DataTable",
    "props": {
      "rows": [{ "id": "1", "name": "Alice" }],
      "pageSize": 10
    },
    "surface": "default"
  }
}
```

```json [Success]
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": "tc-1",
  "result": {
    "componentId": "dt-sess9f8e-01HK9X",
    "channel": "dt-sess9f8e-01HK9X",
    "schema": { "...": "..." },
    "events": ["row_selected"]
  }
}
```

```json [Error]
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": "tc-1",
  "error": {
    "code": -32003,
    "message": "props_invalid",
    "data": { "details": ["required: rows"] }
  }
}
```
::

Error codes occupy the namespace `-32001` through `-32010`. Standard MCP errors (`-32700` parse, `-32600` invalid request, `-32601` method not found, `-32603` internal) are honored but are not GenicUI-specific. The full table lives in [MCP Tools › Error codes](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/mcp-tools#error-codes).

## End-to-end sequence: render a component

```text
┌────────┐                ┌────────┐                ┌────────┐
│ Agent  │                │ Server │                │ Client │
└───┬────┘                └────┬───┘                └────┬───┘
    │  render_component       │                         │
    │ ──────────────────────► │  validate props         │
    │                          │  allocate componentId  │
    │                          │  emit STATE_SNAPSHOT   │
    │                          │ ──────────────────────►│
    │                          │  emit COMPONENT_MOUNTED│
    │                          │ ──────────────────────►│
    │                          │                         │ mount Web Component
    │                          │ ◄──────────────────────│ client.hello (subscribe)
    │                          │                         │
    │  TOOL_CALL_RESULT        │                         │
    │ ◄────────────────────── │                         │
    │                          │                         │
```

Frames flow:

1. **Agent → Server** on `__mcp__`: `TOOL_CALL_STARTED` (seq N), `TOOL_CALL_ARGS` (seq N+1), `TOOL_CALL_RESULT` (seq N+2).
2. **Server → Client** on `<componentId>`: `STATE_SNAPSHOT` (seq 1), `COMPONENT_MOUNTED` (seq 2).
3. **Client → Server** on `<componentId>`: `client.hello` (seq 3) — establishes the reverse subscription.
4. **Server → Agent** on `__agent__`: tool result frame mirroring the JSON-RPC response.

The five events in steps 1 and the two events in step 2 are the AG-UI-required surface for a successful tool call. Skipping any of them breaks client reconnection logic and AG-UI-native consumers (CopilotKit, LangGraph).

## Versioning

The `v` field is the protocol version. Today only `"1"` is defined. Future major versions will increment `v` and ship a parallel subprotocol negotiation. Until then, frames with `v: "1"` are the only valid wire format — anything else closes the socket with WS code 1003.

## What's next

- **Channel multiplexing** — see [Frames](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/frames) for the per-channel `seq` counter, reserved channel names, and out-of-order buffering.
- **Tool contracts** — see [MCP Tools](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/mcp-tools) for the full input/output schemas of all four public tools.
- **Production wiring** — see [Guides › Production](https://genicui.vaah.ai/guides/production) for how `v`, `channel`, and `type` show up in a real Cloudflare Workers deployment.


# Frames

A single WebSocket carries up to 256 channels — one per mounted component plus three reserved system channels. Each channel has its own monotonic `seq` counter, its own subscriber list, and its own replay buffer. This page describes how frames route, how out-of-order delivery is reconciled, and how the server deduplicates retries.

## Channel model

Every GenicUI WebSocket carries a fixed channel set:

| Channel         | Purpose                                                  | Who emits       |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- |
| `__session__`   | Session handshake + heartbeats                           | server only     |
| `__mcp__`       | Tool calls, tool results, JSON-RPC envelopes             | server + agent  |
| `__agent__`     | Agent-to-server responses (rare; mostly server-mediated) | server mediated |
| `<componentId>` | One per mounted component                                | server + client |

`<componentId>` follows the form `<short>-<sessionSuffix>-<ulid>` — for example, `dt-sess9f8e-01HK9X`. The prefix encodes the registry component (`dt` = DataTable), the session suffix scopes the mount, and the ULID guarantees uniqueness across the cluster.

::callout{type="warning"}
The three reserved channels (

`__session__`

, 

`__mcp__`

, 

`__agent__`

) are checked at mount time. Reusing one as a component channel returns 

`-32008 surface_unavailable`

 and closes the allocation.
::

The 256-channel cap is enforced server-side. Opening the 257th channel returns `-32001 component_not_found` and emits `channel.closed` for the would-be channel — the existing 256 channels stay open.

## Frame envelope schema

`Source: packages/core/src/index.ts` exports the canonical `FrameEnvelopeSchema` (TypeBox-derived JSON Schema 2020-12):

```ts
import { Type, type Static } from '@sinclair/typebox';

export const FrameEnvelopeSchema = Type.Object({
  v: Type.Literal(1),
  channel: Type.String({ minLength: 1, maxLength: 128, pattern: '^[\\x21-\\x7E]+$' }),
  type: Type.String({ minLength: 1, maxLength: 64 }),
  payload: Type.Unknown(),
  seq: Type.Integer({ minimum: 0, maximum: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER }),
});

export type FrameEnvelope = Static<typeof FrameEnvelopeSchema>;
```

Key invariants:

- `v` is locked to `1` until a future protocol version ships.
- `channel` rejects any control character — no newlines, no NULs.
- `payload` is `unknown` because the per-type payload schema lives in the event catalog.
- `seq` is uint64; in JavaScript that's bounded to `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (2^53 − 1) since sequences above that risk float drift.

## Sequence ordering

Every channel carries a monotonic `seq` counter that the server increments per emit. The counter resets to `1` on mount and runs until `channel.closed`.

```text
  seq 1   STATE_SNAPSHOT     { state: { rows: [] } }
  seq 2   COMPONENT_MOUNTED  { schema, initialState }
  seq 3   client.hello       (from client → server)
  seq 4   STATE_DELTA        { patch: [{ op: 'add', path: '/rows/-', value: {...} }] }
  seq 5   COMPONENT_EVENT    { action: 'row_selected', detail: { rowId: '2' } }
  seq 6   channel.closed     { reason: 'agent_unmount' }
```

### Out-of-order buffering

Frames may arrive out of order — TCP can reorder, and intermediate proxies may delay a `seq 5` behind a `seq 7`. The client buffers per-channel until `seq` is contiguous:

```text
  received seqs: 3, 4, 7, 5, 6
  ─► contiguous from 3 → apply 3, 4
  ─► 5 and 6 held; 7 buffered
  ─► on arrival of 5: apply 5, 6
  ─► on arrival of 6: apply 6, then 7
  ─► invariant: application is always in seq order, never arrival order
```

The buffer is bounded per channel — 500 frames in F33's session buffer. Exceeding the bound closes the socket with WS code 1013 (try again later) and forces the client to reconnect with `Last-Event-ID`.

### Hard rule: STATE\_DELTA before COMPONENT\_EVENT

When state and an event happen in the same logical step, the server **always** emits `STATE_DELTA` before any `COMPONENT_EVENT` that observes that state. The client guarantees causal consistency this way — by the time the event reaches the agent, the row the agent clicked is already updated.

## Idempotency keys

`render_component` and `update_component` accept an optional `clientRequestId` (UUID v4) that the server caches for 24 hours. Retries with the same `id` return the original response without re-executing the tool:

```text
Agent: render_component { name: "DataTable", props: {...}, clientRequestId: "r-1" }
Server: { componentId: "dt-...", ... }    ← 200 OK, cached

Agent: render_component { name: "DataTable", props: {...}, clientRequestId: "r-1" }   ← retry
Server: { componentId: "dt-...", ... }    ← SAME response, no re-mount
```

The cache key is `(apiKey, clientRequestId)` — one agent's idempotency namespace never collides with another's. The 24h TTL is enforced by an LRU; old keys are evicted silently.

::callout{type="info"}
Idempotency is the primary defense against the Claude Code MCP retry loop. When the network hiccups mid-render, the wrapper retries the same 

`render_component`

 with the same 

`clientRequestId`

. Without idempotency, a retry would allocate a second 

`componentId`

 and double-mount.
::

## Channel lifecycle

```text
  ┌─────────────┐  render_component  ┌─────────────┐
  │ (no channel)│ ─────────────────► │  reserved   │
  └─────────────┘                    └──────┬──────┘
                                             │ STATE_SNAPSHOT + COMPONENT_MOUNTED
                                             ▼
                                       ┌─────────────┐
                                       │   mounted   │◄──── client.hello
                                       └──────┬──────┘
                                              │
                          ┌───────────────────┼─────────────────────┐
                          ▼                   ▼                     ▼
                  ┌──────────────┐    ┌──────────────┐       ┌──────────────┐
                  │ update_comp  │    │ subscribe_to │       │ unmount_comp │
                  │ → STATE_DELTA│    │   _events    │       │ → close      │
                  └──────────────┘    └──────────────┘       └──────┬───────┘
                          │                   │                     │
                          └───────────────────┴─────────────────────┘
                                              ▼
                                       ┌─────────────┐
                                       │  closing    │
                                       └──────┬──────┘
                                              │ channel.closed
                                              ▼
                                       (channel gone)
```

The closing state is terminal — a closed channel cannot be reopened. To re-mount, the agent calls `render_component` again and gets a fresh `componentId`.

## Validation at the wire

Frames failing validation close the socket with WS code 1003 (unsupported data). The check order:

1. Single-line JSON parses.
2. `v === 1`.
3. `channel` matches the allowed pattern.
4. `type` is in the AG-UI/GenicUI event catalog.
5. `payload` conforms to the event's schema.
6. `seq` is a non-negative integer.

A failure on any step closes with `1003`. There is no half-open state — clients either see the full frame or see the socket die.

## What's next

- **Event semantics** — see [Events](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/events) for how user actions cross the wire back to the agent.
- **Hardening** — see [Trust Boundary](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/trust-boundary) for how the frame validator stops prototype pollution and schema bypass.
- **Production deployment** — see [Guides › Production](https://genicui.vaah.ai/guides/production) for how Cloudflare Workers and Bun self-host handle backpressure at the frame layer.


# MCP Tools

GenicUI exposes exactly four public MCP tools. They are the entire wire protocol from the agent's perspective — every render, update, and event subscription flows through one of them. Each tool's `inputSchema` is emitted with `additionalProperties: false`, and the server validates every call against the locked contract before any state mutates.

## Tool catalog

::tabs
  :::tab{icon="i-lucide-search" label="find_ui_component"}
  Resolve a UI capability to a `ui://` resource.

  ```json
  { "capability": "table", "tags": ["sortable", "filterable"] }
  ```

  Returns the catalog entry (schema + examples + events) so the agent can `resources/read` it.
  :::

  :::tab{icon="i-lucide-package-plus" label="render_component"}
  Mount a component on a connected client.

  ```json
  { "name": "DataTable", "props": { "rows": [...], "pageSize": 10 }, "surface": "default" }
  ```

  Returns a `componentId` and channel. Server emits `STATE_SNAPSHOT` + `COMPONENT_MOUNTED` on that channel.
  :::

  :::tab{icon="i-lucide-refresh-cw" label="update_component"}
  Apply RFC 6902 patches or merge a partial state.

  ```json
  { "componentId": "dt-...", "patches": [{ "op": "replace", "path": "/rows/1/name", "value": "Alicia" }] }
  ```

  Server emits `STATE_DELTA` with the applied op list. Falls back to `STATE_SNAPSHOT` if patches fail.
  :::

  :::tab{icon="i-lucide-bell" label="subscribe_to_events"}
  Receive user-driven events from a mounted component.

  ```json
  { "componentId": "dt-...", "events": ["row_selected"] }
  ```

  Server returns a `subscriptionId` and starts forwarding matching `COMPONENT_EVENT` frames.
  :::
::

## Error codes

Every GenicUI tool error occupies the namespace `-32001` through `-32010`. Standard MCP errors (`-32700` parse, `-32600` invalid request, `-32601` method not found, `-32603` internal) are honored but not GenicUI-specific.

| Code     | Name                     | When                                                                       |
| -------- | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-32001` | `component_not_found`    | URI / componentId is unknown to the registry.                              |
| `-32002` | `surface_unavailable`    | Reserved channel name (`__session__`, `__mcp__`, `__agent__`).             |
| `-32003` | `props_invalid`          | Props fail TypeBox validation. Includes `data.details[]` with field paths. |
| `-32004` | `patch_invalid`          | Patch op targets a path that doesn't exist in current state.               |
| `-32005` | `event_unknown`          | Subscription `events` filter names an event the component doesn't emit.    |
| `-32006` | `subscription_not_found` | `unsubscribe` references a missing `subscriptionId`.                       |
| `-32007` | `idempotency_conflict`   | Reused `clientRequestId` with different params.                            |
| `-32008` | `surface_unavailable`    | Channel cap reached or reserved channel reused.                            |
| `-32009` | `version_drift`          | Component version drift > 2 minor versions.                                |
| `-32010` | `internal`               | Unrecoverable internal error. Retry is futile; escalate.                   |

`Source: packages/server/src/mcp/error-codes.ts` defines the enum. Each error includes a `data` object with diagnostic context the agent can use to recover.

---

## `find_ui_component`

`Source: .vaahagents/requirements/specs/features/feature-015-find-ui-component-tool.md` (F15)

Resolves a UI capability to a single `ui://` resource. Returns the catalog entry with full schema, examples, and event list so the agent can read it back via MCP's `resources/read`.

### Input schema

```ts
{
  capability: string;       // semantic query, e.g. "table", "form", "chart"
  tags?: string[];          // optional tag filter (intersection)
  topK?: number;            // max results (default 1, max 5)
}
```

### Output schema

```ts
{
  uri: string;              // "ui://components/data-table@1.0.0"
  name: string;             // "DataTable"
  version: string;          // semver
  description: string;
  propsSchema: JSONSchema;  // additionalProperties: false
  events: string[];
  examples: object[];
}
```

### Example

::code-group
```json [Request]
{ "name": "find_ui_component", "arguments": { "capability": "table", "tags": ["sortable"], "topK": 1 } }
```

```json [Response — exact match]
{
  "uri": "ui://components/data-table@1.0.0",
  "name": "DataTable",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "Server-paginated table with sortable headers and per-column filters.",
  "propsSchema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "rows": { "type": "array" },
      "columns": { "type": "array" },
      "pageSize": { "type": "integer", "default": 25 }
    },
    "required": ["rows", "columns"],
    "additionalProperties": false
  },
  "events": ["row_selected", "sort_change", "filter_change"],
  "examples": [{ "rows": [{ "id": "1", "name": "Alice" }], "columns": [{ "key": "name", "label": "Name" }] }]
}
```

```json [Response — no match]
{ "results": [], "reason": "no_component_matches" }
```

```json [Response — ambiguous]
{ "results": [], "disambiguation": [
  { "uri": "ui://components/data-table@1.0.0", "tags": ["sortable", "filterable"] },
  { "uri": "ui://components/grid@1.2.0", "tags": ["filterable", "virtualized"] }
] }
```
::

### Failure modes

- **Empty match** — server returns `{ results: [], reason: 'no_component_matches' }` instead of an error. The agent should broaden the `capability` or drop `tags`.
- **Ambiguous match** — server returns a `disambiguation` array listing every candidate. The agent picks one and retries with a more specific tag.

---

## `render_component`

`Source: .vaahagents/requirements/specs/features/feature-016-render-component-tool.md` (F16)

Validates props against the component's TypeBox schema, allocates a fresh `componentId` + channel, and emits `STATE_SNAPSHOT` followed by `COMPONENT_MOUNTED`. The tool returns once the mount has been emitted; the client's Web Component upgrade happens out-of-band.

### Input schema

```ts
{
  name: string;             // component name (registry-resolved)
  props: object;            // matches the resolved schema
  surface?: string;         // default "default"; multi-surface mounting
  clientRequestId?: string; // idempotency key (UUID v4)
  componentVersion?: string; // pinned version; default = latest
}
```

### Output schema

```ts
{
  componentId: string;      // "dt-sess9f8e-01HK9X"
  channel: string;          // mirrors componentId
  schema: JSONSchema;       // resolved schema (for the agent's records)
  events: string[];         // emitted events the agent may subscribe to
}
```

### Example

::code-group
```json [Request]
{
  "name": "render_component",
  "arguments": {
    "name": "DataTable",
    "props": {
      "rows": [{ "id": "1", "name": "Alice" }],
      "columns": [{ "key": "name", "label": "Name" }],
      "pageSize": 10
    },
    "surface": "default",
    "clientRequestId": "r-1"
  }
}
```

```json [Response]
{
  "componentId": "dt-sess9f8e-01HK9X",
  "channel": "dt-sess9f8e-01HK9X",
  "schema": { "type": "object", "additionalProperties": false, "...": "..." },
  "events": ["row_selected", "sort_change", "filter_change"]
}
```

```json [Error — props_invalid]
{
  "isError": true,
  "content": [{
    "type": "text",
    "text": "{\"code\":-32003,\"message\":\"props_invalid\",\"data\":{\"details\":[\"required: rows\"]}}"
  }]
}
```
::

### Failure modes

- `-32003 props_invalid` — props fail TypeBox validation. Includes `data.details[]` with field paths.
- `-32001 component_not_found` — `name` is not in the registry.
- `-32008 surface_unavailable` — channel cap reached.
- `-32007 idempotency_conflict` — `clientRequestId` reused with different params.

### Idempotency

Pass `clientRequestId: "<uuid>"` and the server caches the response for 24 hours. Retries with the same id return the original `componentId` without re-mounting — see [Frames › Idempotency keys](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/frames#idempotency-keys).

---

## `update_component`

`Source: .vaahagents/requirements/specs/features/feature-017-update-component-tool.md` (F17)

Accepts either `patches` (RFC 6902 JSON-Patch) or `mode: 'replace'` with full props. The server diffs current state vs new state, validates, and emits either `STATE_DELTA` or `STATE_SNAPSHOT` (when patches fail or full replacement is requested).

### Input schema

```ts
{
  componentId: string;
  patches?: JsonPatchOp[];          // discriminated union: patches XOR mode
  mode?: 'replace';                 // full snapshot replacement
  props?: object;                   // required when mode = 'replace'
  clientRequestId?: string;
}
```

### Output schema

```ts
{
  componentId: string;
  channel: string;
  applied: boolean;                 // false → server fell back to STATE_SNAPSHOT
  diff: {
    patched?: JsonPatchOp[];        // applied ops (success path)
    snapshot?: object;              // full state (fallback path)
  };
}
```

### Example — patches (primary)

::code-group
```json [Request]
{
  "name": "update_component",
  "arguments": {
    "componentId": "dt-sess9f8e-01HK9X",
    "patches": [
      { "op": "replace", "path": "/rows/0/name", "value": "Alicia" },
      { "op": "add", "path": "/rows/-", "value": { "id": "2", "name": "Bob" } }
    ]
  }
}
```

```json [Response]
{
  "componentId": "dt-sess9f8e-01HK9X",
  "channel": "dt-sess9f8e-01HK9X",
  "applied": true,
  "diff": {
    "patched": [
      { "op": "replace", "path": "/rows/0/name", "value": "Alicia" },
      { "op": "add", "path": "/rows/1", "value": { "id": "2", "name": "Bob" } }
    ]
  }
}
```
::

### Example — replace (full snapshot)

::code-group
```json [Request]
{
  "name": "update_component",
  "arguments": {
    "componentId": "dt-sess9f8e-01HK9X",
    "mode": "replace",
    "props": { "rows": [{ "id": "1", "name": "Alice" }], "columns": [], "pageSize": 25 }
  }
}
```

```json [Response]
{
  "componentId": "dt-sess9f8e-01HK9X",
  "channel": "dt-sess9f8e-01HK9X",
  "applied": true,
  "diff": { "snapshot": { "rows": [...], "columns": [], "pageSize": 25 } }
}
```
::

### Failure modes

- `-32004 patch_invalid` — patch op targets a path not in current state.
- `-32003 props_invalid` — `mode: 'replace'` props fail TypeBox validation.
- `-32001 component_not_found` — `componentId` is not currently mounted.
- Both `patches` and `mode: 'replace'` together → `-32003 props_invalid` (discriminated union).

### Concurrency

Concurrent `update_component` calls on the same `componentId` are serialized by a per-component lock (F29). Two racing calls are applied in arrival order — never torn, never interleaved.

---

## `subscribe_to_events`

`Source: .vaahagents/requirements/specs/features/feature-018-subscribe-to-events-tool.md` (F18)

Returns a `subscriptionId` and starts forwarding matching `COMPONENT_EVENT` frames back to the agent. Subscriptions are scoped to one component and an optional event-name filter.

### Input schema

```ts
{
  componentId: string;
  events?: string[];     // omit = subscribe to all events for the component
}
```

### Output schema

```ts
{
  subscriptionId: string; // "sub-9c2a"
  componentId: string;
  events: string[];       // resolved filter (or "*" if all)
}
```

### Server push (subsequent)

```json
{
  "v": 1,
  "channel": "__mcp__",
  "type": "EVENT",
  "payload": {
    "subscriptionId": "sub-9c2a",
    "componentId": "dt-sess9f8e-01HK9X",
    "event": "row_selected",
    "data": { "rowId": "1" }
  },
  "seq": 14
}
```

### Example

::code-group
```json [Request]
{ "name": "subscribe_to_events", "arguments": { "componentId": "dt-sess9f8e-01HK9X", "events": ["row_selected"] } }
```

```json [Response]
{ "subscriptionId": "sub-9c2a", "componentId": "dt-sess9f8e-01HK9X", "events": ["row_selected"] }
```
::

### Failure modes

- `-32005 event_unknown` — `events` filter names an event the component doesn't emit.
- `-32001 component_not_found` — `componentId` is not currently mounted.
- `-32006 subscription_not_found` — `unsubscribe` references a missing `subscriptionId`.

### Auto-cleanup

When a component unmounts (`unmount_component` or session teardown), every subscription against it auto-closes with `subscription.closed`. The agent never needs to clean up explicitly.

---

## Tool wiring cheatsheet

| Tool                  | Reads                 | Writes            | Emits (wire)                           |
| --------------------- | --------------------- | ----------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `find_ui_component`   | registry              | —                 | none (RPC only)                        |
| `render_component`    | registry, propsSchema | componentStore    | `STATE_SNAPSHOT` + `COMPONENT_MOUNTED` |
| `update_component`    | current state         | componentStore    | `STATE_DELTA` or `STATE_SNAPSHOT`      |
| `subscribe_to_events` | subscriptionStore     | subscriptionStore | filtered `COMPONENT_EVENT` pushes      |

Every tool call also emits the AG-UI run lifecycle frames (`RUN_STARTED` → `TOOL_CALL_STARTED` → `TOOL_CALL_ARGS` → `TOOL_CALL_RESULT` → `RUN_FINISHED`) on the `__mcp__` channel. AG-UI-native consumers (CopilotKit, LangGraph) consume those frames as-is — no GenicUI-specific adaptation needed.

## What's next

- **Schema validation** — see [Trust Boundary](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/trust-boundary) for how `Value.Check()`, prototype-pollution stripping, and `additionalProperties: false` harden every tool call.
- **Component lifecycle** — see [Components](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/components) for the Web Component base class that consumes `STATE_SNAPSHOT` and `STATE_DELTA`.
- **Event semantics** — see [Events](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/events) for what happens between `subscribe_to_events` and `COMPONENT_EVENT`.
- **Implementation** — see [API Reference › Server](https://genicui.vaah.ai/api/server) for the handler code and `AgentBridge` schema.


# Components

Every GenicUI component is a Web Component — a `customElements.define`-registered class extending `GenicElement` from `@genicui/runtime`. The runtime engine mounts it inside a closed Shadow DOM, applies patches to its `props` attribute, and tears it down when the server emits `channel.closed`. This page is the lifecycle reference.

## Web Component lifecycle

A GenicUI component follows the standard custom-element lifecycle, but the runtime drives each callback. The five phases below describe a single mount-and-patch flow.

::steps
### `constructor()`

Runs once when the element is created. The runtime constructs the element with `new MyEl()`, captures any synchronous setup, and attaches a closed Shadow Root via `attachShadow({ mode: 'closed' })`. After construction, no further setup runs — the element is inert until it's added to the DOM.

### `connectedCallback()`

Fires when the element is appended to a parent. The runtime calls this when a `STATE_SNAPSHOT` arrives for a fresh `componentId`. Inside, the base class reads the `props` attribute, applies the initial state to the Shadow DOM, and emits a `client.hello` frame back to the server to establish the reverse subscription.

### `attributeChangedCallback()`

Fires when any attribute in `observedAttributes` changes. The base class observes `props`, `component-id`, and `surface` — when `props` changes (because a `STATE_DELTA` arrived), the runtime diffs the JSON-serialized prop tree and calls the element's `onPatch()` method with the patch list. The element re-renders only the changed sub-tree.

### `disconnectedCallback()`

Fires when the element is removed. The runtime calls this when `channel.closed` arrives. The base class tears down internal listeners, emits `channel.closed` to confirm teardown, and disposes the channel handler.

### `adoptedCallback()`

Runs when the element is moved to a new document. GenicUI does not currently support cross-document adoption — the runtime ignores this callback. Components moved between roots within the same document retain their channel.
::

## Why closed Shadow DOM

GenicUI uses `attachShadow({ mode: 'closed' })` for every component. The trade-off is intentional:

- **No global CSS bleed.** Page-level styles cannot pierce the Shadow boundary, and component styles cannot leak out. PrimeVue's scoped CSS, Mantine's design tokens, and shadcn's Tailwind reset all stay where they belong.
- **No accidental introspection.** Page scripts cannot reach into the shadow root via `element.shadowRoot`. The runtime is the only path in, via the closed reference held inside the base class.
- **Composable with any framework.** PrimeVue 4's PassThrough API hooks mount points without DOM probing; Vue, React, and Solid components can sit inside without prop-drilling through the boundary.

::callout{type="warning"}
The 

`mode: 'closed'`

 choice is locked in F21 and codified in the implementation. Components that try to re-open the Shadow Root break the contract — agents and registries cannot assume any element exposes 

`shadowRoot`

.
::

## The `GenicElement` base class

`Source: packages/client/src/web-component/genetic-element.ts` exports the base class. Every registry component extends it.

```ts
import { GenicElement } from '@genicui/runtime';

class DataTableElement extends GenicElement {
  static get observedAttributes() {
    return ['props', 'component-id', 'surface'];
  }

  connectedCallback() {
    super.connectedCallback();   // attaches closed shadow, parses props
    this.update(this.props);    // initial render
  }

  onPatch(patches: JsonPatchOp[]) {
    // Diff-paint: only re-render the changed sub-tree.
    for (const op of patches) this.applyOp(op);
  }

  onEvent(name: string, detail: unknown) {
    // Bubble composed events up to the runtime.
    this.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent(name, { detail, bubbles: true, composed: true }));
  }
}

customElements.define('genic-data-table', DataTableElement);
```

The base class provides:

- **Reactive props** — `get props()` returns the JSON-parsed `props` attribute and triggers `onPatch()` whenever the attribute mutates.
- **Lifecycle hooks** — `connectedCallback`, `disconnectedCallback`, `attributeChangedCallback` already wired; subclasses override `onPatch` and `onEvent`.
- **Event bubbling** — any `composed: true` CustomEvent dispatched inside the Shadow DOM reaches the runtime listener on the document.

## Observed attributes

Every GenicUI element observes three attributes:

| Attribute      | Type        | Purpose                                                           |
| -------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `props`        | JSON string | Serialized component props. Updates drive re-render.              |
| `component-id` | string      | The channel key. Set once at mount; never mutated.                |
| `surface`      | string      | Mount surface (`default`, `chat-panel`, etc.). Set once at mount. |

Only `props` mutates over a component's lifetime. The runtime encodes each `STATE_DELTA` as a `props` attribute mutation with a custom event to trigger `attributeChangedCallback`. The base class's `get props()` re-parses the JSON and `onPatch()` receives the diff.

## The runtime engine

`Source: packages/client/src/index.ts` exports `createRuntime`. The runtime is a module-isolated sub-module (F29-AC4) that mounts, patches, and tears down components.

```ts
import { createRuntime } from '@genicui/client';

const rt = createRuntime({
  socket,         // GenicClient WebSocket
  registry,       // component registry (loaded by Vite plugin)
  sessionStore,   // SessionStore for last-event-id replay
});

rt.onMessage(frame);   // routes frame → mount / patch / unmount / event
```

The runtime's job:

1. Receive a frame from `GenicClient`.
2. Switch on `frame.type`:
   - `STATE_SNAPSHOT` → resolve the registry entry, instantiate the element, append to the DOM, dispatch a synthetic attribute change.
   - `STATE_DELTA` → resolve the patch list against the live element, set the `props` attribute.
   - `COMPONENT_EVENT` (from the server) → forward to the agent via `__mcp__`.
   - `channel.closed` → remove the element from the DOM, dispose handlers.
3. Emit outbound frames for `client.hello` and `COMPONENT_EVENT` back to the server.

The runtime is **module-isolated** — it sets no globals on `window`. Test it with `import { createRuntime } from '@genicui/client'` and you get a fresh instance per call.

## Mount and patch timing budgets

The runtime enforces two timing budgets. Failing either closes the channel with WS code 1011 (internal error):

| Frame                        | Budget  | Source  |
| ---------------------------- | ------- | ------- |
| `STATE_SNAPSHOT` → DOM mount | ≤ 50 ms | F29-AC1 |
| `STATE_DELTA` → DOM patch    | ≤ 10 ms | F29-AC2 |

These budgets assume a typical PrimeVue DataTable mount. Heavy frameworks or large initial states may exceed them — registries with large prop payloads should consider lazy loading or `STATE_SNAPSHOT` chunking (Phase 2).

## Mount and patch flow

```text
              ┌────────────────────────┐
              │ GenicClient.onMessage  │
              └──────────┬─────────────┘
                         ▼
              ┌────────────────────────┐
              │ runtime.onMessage      │
              └──────────┬─────────────┘
                         ▼
            ┌────────────────────────────┐
            │ switch (frame.type)         │
            └──────────┬──────────────────┘
                       │
       ┌───────────────┼────────────────┐
       ▼               ▼                ▼
 STATE_SNAPSHOT   STATE_DELTA     channel.closed
       │               │                │
       ▼               ▼                ▼
  new MyEl()    setAttribute('props',  parent.removeChild(el)
  attachShadow  JSON.stringify(state))    dispose
  append to DOM attributeChangedCallback
  setAttribute  → onPatch(patches)
  → update()    → applyOp per op
```

## PassThrough API (PrimeVue 4)

The PrimeVue 4 registry uses PrimeVue's PassThrough API to wire event handlers and props without DOM probing. Each GenicUI component extends the base `GenicElement`, then in its `onPatch` it forwards props to the underlying PrimeVue component instance through a `pt` (pass-through) object:

```ts
// Source: registries/primevue/src/data-table.ts
import PrimeVueDataTable from 'primevue/datatable';

onPatch(patches: JsonPatchOp[]) {
  for (const op of patches) {
    const [key, value] = applyOp(this.props, op);
    this.primevueRef.setProp(key, value);   // ← PassThrough
  }
  this.primevueRef.emit('patch-applied');
}
```

The runtime never touches PrimeVue's internals — PrimeVue receives a `MutationObserver`-driven prop change and re-renders itself. The 8-prop `gv-data-table` API wraps PrimeVue's 30+ props down to the smallest set agents need.

## Unmount cleanup

When the agent calls `unmount_component` (internal tool, F19) or the session tears down, the runtime:

1. Receives `channel.closed` on the component's channel.
2. Calls `parent.removeChild(el)` — fires `disconnectedCallback`.
3. The base class removes event listeners and clears the `props` cache.
4. The runtime removes the channel handler from `GenicClient`'s subscription map.
5. `subscription.closed` fires for every active `subscribe_to_events` against the component.

The component's Web Component instance is garbage-collected once no JS references hold it. No state survives — every mount is fresh.

## What's next

- **Frame-level multiplexing** — see [Frames](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/frames) for the channel and seq mechanics that drive `STATE_SNAPSHOT` and `STATE_DELTA` ordering.
- **User actions** — see [Events](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/events) for the `composed: true` event flow that crosses back from the Shadow DOM to the agent.
- **Catalog** — see [Registries](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/registries) for the `defineRegistry` and `defineComponent` contracts that produce the `<genic-data-table>` element above.
- **Implementation** — see [API Reference › Client](https://genicui.vaah.ai/api/client) for the full `@genicui/client` surface.


# Events

User actions cross three boundaries to reach the agent: the closed Shadow DOM, the WebSocket, and the MCP subscription filter. Each boundary has its own contract. This page walks a click from the user's cursor to the agent's next tool call and explains what can go wrong at each step.

## The `composed: true` decision

A GenicUI element lives inside a closed Shadow DOM. By default, CustomEvents dispatched inside a closed Shadow Root **do not** cross the boundary — they stop at the Shadow Root and never reach `document`. GenicUI's solution is the `composed: true` flag, which forces the event to cross the Shadow boundary:

::code-group
```ts [Inside the component]
// Source: registries/primevue/src/data-table.ts
this.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('row_selected', {
  detail: { rowId: '2' },
  bubbles: true,
  composed: true,   // ← crosses the closed Shadow DOM
}));
```

```ts [Runtime listener — outside the Shadow]
// Source: packages/client/src/runtime/event-bridge.ts
document.addEventListener('row_selected', (e) => {
  const componentId = (e.target as HTMLElement).closest('genic-data-table')?.getAttribute('component-id');
  if (!componentId) return;
  client.send({
    type: 'COMPONENT_EVENT',
    channel: componentId,
    payload: {
      componentId,
      action: e.type,
      detail: e.detail,
    },
  });
}, { capture: true });
```
::

::callout{type="warning"}
Events without 

`composed: true`

 are silently dropped. F19-AC1 enforces this — the runtime's event bridge only forwards events that successfully cross the Shadow boundary. A CommonJS-style dispatcher that forgets the flag will not produce any wire frames.
::

## End-to-end event flow

```text
┌─────────┐         ┌──────────────────┐         ┌─────────┐         ┌─────────┐
│  User   │         │ <genic-data-     │         │ Runtime │         │ Server  │
│  click  │         │  table> Shadow   │         │ event   │         │         │
└────┬────┘         └────────┬─────────┘         └────┬────┘         └────┬────┘
     │ click row #2          │                          │                   │
     │ ─────────────────────►│ PrimeVue @row-click      │                   │
     │                       │ Vue shim dispatches       │                   │
     │                       │ CustomEvent(              │                   │
     │                       │   'row_selected',         │                   │
     │                       │   { detail, composed:true } )              │
     │                       │ ─────────────────────────►                   │
     │                       │                          │ bridges to wire:   │
     │                       │                          │ COMPONENT_EVENT    │
     │                       │                          │ ──────────────────►│
     │                       │                          │                   │ validate,
     │                       │                          │                   │ route to subscribers,
     │                       │                          │                   │ forward to agent
     │                       │                          │                   │ ──► MCP __agent__
```

The five steps in detail:

1. **User clicks row** inside the Shadow DOM.
2. **PrimeVue** emits its native `@row-click` Vue event.
3. **Vue shim** (`packages/client/src/vue/`) translates it to a `CustomEvent('row_selected', { detail, composed: true })`.
4. **Runtime event bridge** catches the event at the document level (capture phase), serializes the payload, and emits a `COMPONENT_EVENT` frame on the WebSocket.
5. **Server** validates the payload against the component's event schema, routes it to subscribers, and forwards to the agent's MCP stream.

## `COMPONENT_EVENT` payload schema

`Source: .vaahagents/requirements/specs/features/feature-019-event-capture-forwarding.md`

```ts
{
  v: 1;
  channel: string;        // componentId
  type: 'COMPONENT_EVENT';
  payload: {
    componentId: string;  // mirrors channel
    action: string;       // event name (e.g. 'row_selected')
    detail: unknown;      // JSON-serializable payload from the CustomEvent
  };
  seq: number;            // monotonic per channel
}
```

The `detail` field is `unknown` at the wire level — the runtime passes whatever the Web Component dispatched. The server validates against the per-component event schema declared in the registry (`events.<name>.payloadSchema`).

## `subscribe_to_events` filtering

`Source: .vaahagents/requirements/specs/features/feature-018-subscribe-to-events-tool.md`

Subscriptions are scoped to one component plus an optional event-name filter. A subscription without `events` receives every event the component emits.

| Subscription `events`             | What the agent receives         |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `["row_selected"]`                | only `row_selected`             |
| `["row_selected", "sort_change"]` | both, separately framed         |
| omitted                           | every event the component emits |

The runtime never filters at the client — every event the bridge catches is sent on the wire, and the server applies the filter before forwarding to the agent. This keeps the client logic simple and centralizes policy server-side.

## Lifecycle: subscribe, receive, unsubscribe

```text
  Agent                              Server                          Component
    │  subscribe_to_events             │                                │
    │ ───────────────────────────────►│                                │
    │  { subscriptionId: "sub-9c2a" } │                                │
    │ ◄───────────────────────────────│                                │
    │                                  │                                │
    │                                  │     user clicks row            │
    │                                  │ ◄──────────────────────────────│
    │                                  │ validate, route                │
    │  COMPONENT_EVENT                 │                                │
    │ ◄───────────────────────────────│                                │
    │  { rowId: '2' }                  │                                │
    │                                  │                                │
    │  unsubscribe { sub-9c2a }        │                                │
    │ ───────────────────────────────►│                                │
    │                                  │ drop subscription              │
    │                                  │                                │
    │                                  │     component unmounts         │
    │                                  │ ◄──────────────────────────────│
    │  subscription.closed             │                                │
    │ ◄───────────────────────────────│  ← auto-cleanup                │
```

Three termination paths:

- **Explicit unsubscribe** — `unsubscribe` with the `subscriptionId`. Server drops the subscription; no further events flow.
- **Component unmount** — `unmount_component` or session teardown. Server emits `subscription.closed` with `reason: 'component_unmount'` and drops state.
- **Session close** — WebSocket disconnects. All subscriptions for that session die with the connection.

## Error handling

Malformed events (invalid payload, schema mismatch) are dropped, not rejected. The server logs a warning with the `componentId`, the event name, and the validation error, and increments a `drop_count` counter visible to operators.

| Symptom                                           | Server action                               |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| Event payload fails `events.<name>.payloadSchema` | Drop + log warning + increment `drop_count` |
| Event name not in component's `events[]`          | Drop + log warning                          |
| Component not mounted                             | Drop silently                               |
| Channel queue overflow (> 500 frames)             | Close socket with WS code 1013              |

::callout{type="info"}
The server never returns 

`-32004`

 for a malformed event — that's reserved for 

`update_component`

 patch failures. Event failures are silent by design: the agent should not retry a user click that the server has already dropped. See 

[Trust Boundary › Drop vs Reject](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/trust-boundary#drop-vs-reject)

 for the rationale.
::

## Backpressure and rate limits

The internal event bus (F20) caps each socket's outbound queue at **500 frames**. When the queue overflows, the socket closes with WS code 1013 (try again later). The client reconnects with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, 30s cap) and replays from `Last-Event-ID`.

A per-component rate limit caps event delivery at **200 events/sec** (F19-AC3). Beyond that, the server drops excess events and increments `drop_count`. Components generating > 200 events/sec (autocomplete dropdowns, drag-tracked sliders) should debounce at the source rather than rely on server throttling.

## What's next

- **Schema validation** — see [Trust Boundary](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/trust-boundary) for the prototype-pollution strip and `additionalProperties: false` enforcement that protects event payloads too.
- **Mount lifecycle** — see [Components](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/components) for the Web Component lifecycle that dispatches these events.
- **Tool contracts** — see [MCP Tools › `subscribe_to_events`](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/mcp-tools#subscribe_to_events) for the request/response shapes and error codes.
- **Production deployment** — see [Guides › Production](https://genicui.vaah.ai/guides/production) for how Cloudflare Durable Objects back the event bus in production.


# Trust Boundary

GenicUI assumes the agent is authenticated but **not trusted**. A valid API key only proves the agent has credentials — it doesn't prove the agent is benevolent. The trust boundary is the input validation pipeline that runs on every tool call before any state mutates. This page is the security reference: where the boundary sits, what it checks, and how it fails.

## Three trust zones

GenicUI has three independent trust boundaries. A breach in one does not auto-breach the next.

```text
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Zone 1 — Network → Server                                  │
│  • TLS termination (Cloudflare / host)                      │
│  • API key validation                                       │
│  • WebSocket subprotocol check                               │
│  Threat: unauthenticated abuse                              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                            ↓ trusted (authenticated) ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Zone 2 — Agent tool call → Server handler                  │
│  • JSON Schema validation (TypeBox Value.Check)            │
│  • Prototype pollution strip                                │
│  • Schema version drift detection                           │
│  • Idempotency key check                                    │
│  Threat: authenticated abuse (agent exceeding authority)    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                            ↓ trusted (validated) ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Zone 3 — User event → Agent                                │
│  • CustomEvent comes from Shadow DOM (less surface)         │
│  • Server-side schema check on payload                      │
│  • Agent must re-validate detail payload                    │
│  Threat: user-injected prompt manipulation                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Zone 1 is the standard network edge — Cloudflare Workers or a reverse proxy. Zone 2 is where the rest of this page focuses. Zone 3 is documented under [Events › Error handling](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/events#error-handling).

## Why three zones

Each zone defends against a different adversary. A single boundary would conflate them:

- Zone 1 stops **unauthenticated** attackers from reaching the agent logic.
- Zone 2 stops **authenticated agents** from doing more than their schema permits — even if Zone 1 trusted them.
- Zone 3 stops **end users** from injecting values that manipulate the agent's next turn.

Separating them means an attacker who breaches Zone 1 still cannot trigger an unschema'd state mutation, and an attacker who breaches Zone 2 still cannot inject events through a user's browser.

## The input validation pipeline

Every inbound tool call runs through five sequential steps. Each step must pass before the next runs.

```text
Raw payload
     │
     ▼
[1] stripProtoKeys()   ──── drop __proto__, constructor, prototype recursively
     │
     ▼
[2] Value.Check()      ──── TypeBox JSON Schema validation
     │
     ▼
[3] Discriminated union ──── update_component: patch XOR merge (not both)
     │
     ▼
[4] Version drift       ──── reject drift > 2 minor versions
     │
     ▼
[5] Idempotency dedupe  ──── 24h LRU keyed by (apiKey, clientRequestId)
     │
     ▼
Tool handler (trusted)
```

| Step | Defends against                                    |
| ---- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | Prototype pollution (CVE-2018-3721, CVE-2019-7609) |
| 2    | Type confusion, missing fields, extra fields       |
| 3    | Conflicting update mechanisms                      |
| 4    | Breaking changes the agent doesn't know about      |
| 5    | Replay attacks                                     |

The steps run in order and any failure short-circuits the rest. A failure on step 2 never reaches step 5 — no idempotency cache pollution from invalid payloads.

## `stripProtoKeys` — the prototype-pollution defense

`Source: packages/server/src/mcp/strip-proto-keys.ts`. Step 1 walks the payload recursively and drops any key named `__proto__`, `constructor`, or `prototype`:

```ts
function stripProtoKeys<T>(obj: T): T {
  if (obj === null || typeof obj !== 'object') return obj;
  if (Array.isArray(obj)) return obj.map(stripProtoKeys) as any;
  const out: any = {};
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(obj)) {
    if (k === '__proto__' || k === 'constructor' || k === 'prototype') continue;
    out[k] = stripProtoKeys(v);
  }
  return out;
}
```

The attack vector it blocks:

```json
// Attacker payload
{
  "props": {
    "rows": [],
    "__proto__": { "isAdmin": true }
  }
}
```

If passed to `Object.assign(target, payload)`, the prototype of `target` would gain `isAdmin: true`, affecting every other `target` instance. `stripProtoKeys` removes the malicious key before any merge happens.

::callout{type="warning"}
This is GenicUI's most-tested attack vector. F14-AC1 runs a fast-check property test with 

**10,000 random payloads**

 containing malicious keys at random depths. Every payload must come out with the dangerous keys absent. The test fails CI if any payload survives.
::

## `additionalProperties: false` enforcement

Two enforcement points, two failure modes.

### Per-tool `inputSchema` — strict at request time

Every MCP tool's `inputSchema` is emitted with `additionalProperties: false` at the wire level. TypeBox's `Value.Check()` rejects any extra field:

```ts
const schema = Type.Object({
  name: Type.String(),
  props: Type.Object({ rows: Type.Array(Type.Any()) }),
}, { additionalProperties: false });

const errors = Value.Errors(schema, payload);
if (errors.length > 0) {
  return { code: -32003, message: 'props_invalid', data: { details: errors.map(e => `${e.path}: ${e.message}`) } };
}
```

### Per-registry `propsSchema` — strict at load time

Registry authors cannot sneak in open schemas. At registry load time, the server walks the schema tree and rejects `additionalProperties: true`:

```ts
function rejectOpenSchemas(schema: TSchema): void {
  if (schema.type === 'object' && schema.additionalProperties === true) {
    throw new RegistryValidationError('additionalProperties: true is forbidden');
  }
  // recurse into properties, items, etc.
}
```

A registry with even one open schema fails to load. The server boots into a "registry invalid" state and refuses to serve any tool calls.

## Drop vs reject

The pipeline distinguishes **drop** (silent discard, log warning) from **reject** (return JSON-RPC error to the agent):

| Failure                       | Action                                        | Visible to agent?                       |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `__proto__` strip             | Drop + log warn                               | No — payload is sanitized transparently |
| TypeBox validation fail       | **Reject** with `-32003 props_invalid`        | Yes — agent sees the error              |
| Discriminated union fail      | **Reject** with `-32003 props_invalid`        | Yes                                     |
| Version drift > 2 minor       | **Reject** with `-32009 version_drift`        | Yes                                     |
| Idempotency conflict          | **Reject** with `-32007 idempotency_conflict` | Yes                                     |
| Schema parse at registry load | **Reject** boot                               | Yes — server fails to start             |
| Open schema at registry load  | **Reject** boot                               | Yes                                     |

The reasoning: agents need to **know** when their input is wrong so they can fix it. They don't need to know when a malicious payload was sanitized — that's the server's job, not theirs.

## Penetration test results

The Testable MVP has been exercised against the standard OWASP attack catalog. Results:

| Attack vector                               | Result                                      | Test                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `__proto__` injection via tool call         | **Blocked** — stripped at step 1            | `tests/integration/trust-boundary.test.ts:F14-AC1` (10K random payloads) |
| `constructor.prototype` chain               | **Blocked** — stripped at step 1            | Same property test                                                       |
| Extra field `{"foo": "bar"}` in props       | **Blocked** — `additionalProperties: false` | `tests/integration/schema-validation.test.ts:F14-AC2`                    |
| Type confusion (`"rows": "not-an-array"`)   | **Blocked** — TypeBox rejects               | Same                                                                     |
| Open-schema registry                        | **Blocked at load** — server refuses boot   | `tests/integration/registry-load.test.ts:F14-AC3`                        |
| Patch op targeting `/does/not/exist`        | **Blocked** — `-32004 patch_invalid`        | `tests/integration/patch-validation.test.ts:F14-AC4`                     |
| API key brute force                         | **Rate-limited** — 50 attempts/5min/IP      | F46 Phase 2 (enforced via Cloudflare WAF)                                |
| Replay attack with reused `clientRequestId` | **Idempotent** — returns original response  | F16-AC3                                                                  |

::callout{type="info"}
The full penetration test report and the 

`SECURITY.md`

 disclosure policy live in 

`.vaahagents/requirements/specs/security.md`

 §Security Verification. Bug bounty is Phase 3 — after MVP ships + 50+ GitHub stars.
::

## Threat mitigations matrix (excerpt)

| Threat                    | Mitigation                                                  | Status                         |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| Network sniffing          | TLS termination                                             | Host responsibility            |
| API key brute force       | 128-bit entropy + rate limits                               | MVP partial (Phase 2 enforced) |
| Replay attack             | TLS + WS upgrade auth                                       | MVP                            |
| Prototype pollution       | `stripProtoKeys` + `Object.create(null)` + frozen objects   | MVP                            |
| Schema bypass             | TypeBox + `additionalProperties: false`                     | MVP                            |
| Type confusion            | TypeBox + runtime discriminated union                       | MVP                            |
| XSS in event detail       | `composed: true` events JSON-serialized; agent re-validates | MVP                            |
| Registry supply chain     | npm `--provenance` + conformance tests + manual review      | MVP partial                    |
| Denial of service         | WS heartbeat + max connections per key                      | MVP partial                    |
| User input → agent prompt | Agent must re-validate every event payload                  | Out of MVP scope               |

The full matrix covers 15 threats. The ones deferred to Phase 2 are explicitly tagged — these are *deliberate* gaps, not oversights.

## What's next

- **Schema contracts** — see [Registries](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/registries) for the `defineRegistry` + `defineComponent` shape that the trust boundary validates.
- **Tool contracts** — see [MCP Tools › Error codes](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/mcp-tools#error-codes) for the full -32001..-32010 namespace.
- **Wire-level hardening** — see [Protocol](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/protocol) for the frame validator and WS code 1003 rejection.
- **Production deployment** — see [Guides › Production](https://genicui.vaah.ai/guides/production) for how Cloudflare WAF rules enforce rate limits at the network edge.


# Registries

A **registry** is an npm package that declares a set of components — their schemas, events, tags, and runtime adapters. GenicUI loads one or more registries at boot, validates every schema, and merges them into a single in-memory catalog. This page is the registry contract reference: the shape of a component entry, the URI grammar that identifies it, and the resolution order that wins on conflicts.

## The registry contract

`Source: .vaahagents/requirements/specs/features/feature-037-component-registry.md` (F37)

A registry exports a single object via `defineRegistry()`. Each component entry declares everything the agent needs to discover, validate, and render it.

```ts
import { defineRegistry, defineComponent } from '@genicui/core';

const DataTable = defineComponent({
  name: 'data-table',
  version: '1.0.0',
```
