```ts
  description: 'Server-paginated table with sortable headers and per-column filters.',
  propsSchema: {
    type: 'object',
    properties: {
      rows: { type: 'array' },
      columns: { type: 'array' },
      pageSize: { type: 'integer', default: 25 },
    },
    required: ['rows', 'columns'],
    additionalProperties: false,
  },
  tags: ['table', 'sortable', 'filterable'],
  events: [
    {
      name: 'row_selected',
      payloadSchema: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: { rowId: { type: 'string' } },
        required: ['rowId'],
        additionalProperties: false,
      },
    },
  ],
  examples: [
    {
      rows: [{ id: '1', name: 'Alice' }],
      columns: [{ key: 'name', label: 'Name' }],
    },
  ],
  whenToUse: 'Use this whenever the user wants to see a list of structured records.',
});

export const primevueRegistry = defineRegistry({
  library: '@genicul-primevue/registry',
  version: '1.0.0',
  components: [DataTable],
});
```

The locked contract — every entry must have these fields:

| Field         | Type           | Required | Notes                                               |
| ------------- | -------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`        | string         | ✅        | Registry-unique kebab-case name.                    |
| `version`     | semver         | ✅        | Pinned via npm version.                             |
| `description` | string         | ✅        | One-line summary shown to the agent.                |
| `propsSchema` | JSON Schema    | ✅        | Must include `additionalProperties: false`.         |
| `tags`        | string []      | optional | Discovery hints for `find_ui_component`.            |
| `events`      | `EventEntry[]` | ✅        | Every event the component emits.                    |
| `examples`    | `object[]`     | ✅        | At least one valid props example.                   |
| `whenToUse`   | string         | optional | Agent-facing directive — phrased as an instruction. |

## `ui://` URI grammar

`Source: .vaahagents/requirements/specs/features/feature-024-ui-resource-grammar.md` (F24). Two URI namespaces identify components on the wire:

| Pattern                                   | Type               | Example                                        |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `ui://genicul/{lib}/{comp}`               | **Catalog**        | `ui://genicul/primevue/data-table`             |
| `ui://genicul/{lib}/{comp}@{version}`     | **Catalog pinned** | `ui://genicul/primevue/data-table@1.0.0`       |
| `ui://instance/{sessionId}/{componentId}` | **Live instance**  | `ui://instance/sess-9f8e7d/dt-sess9f8e-01HK9X` |

**Catalog URIs** resolve to the component's metadata — schema, examples, whenToUse — returned via MCP's `resources/read`:

```json
{
  "uri": "ui://genicul/primevue/data-table",
  "mimeType": "application/vnd.genicul.component+json",
  "text": "{ \"schema\": {...}, \"whenToUse\": \"...\", \"examples\": [...] }"
}
```

**Instance URIs** resolve to the live Web Component HTML, served for iframe-mode adapters and SSR previews:

```json
{
  "uri": "ui://instance/sess-9f8e7d/dt-sess9f8e-01HK9X",
  "mimeType": "text/html",
  "text": "<genic-data-table component-id=\"dt-sess9f8e-01HK9X\" props-json=\"...\"></genic-data-table>"
}
```

Malformed URIs return MCP's standard `resource not found` error. There is no partial match — `ui://genicul/primevue` (no component) is invalid.

## Trust tiers and resolution order

`Source: .vaahagents/requirements/specs/features/feature-038-registry-trust-tiers.md` (F38). GenicUI loads registries from three tiers:

| Tier        | Source               | Path                                         | Allow-list?                            |
| ----------- | -------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| **Project** | Repo-local manifest  | `./registry.json` or `registries/` directory | No — always trusted                    |
| **User**    | User home directory  | `~/.config/genicui/registry.json`            | No                                     |
| **Remote**  | HTTP registry server | `https://<registry-host>/api/components`     | **Yes** — `GENICUI_REGISTRY_ALLOWLIST` |

Resolution order: **Project > User > Remote**. When two tiers define the same component URI, the higher tier wins:

```text
Project registry:  data-table@1.0.0 (custom props)
User registry:     data-table@2.0.0
Remote registry:   data-table@2.0.0 (official)
                   ─────────────────
Effective:         data-table@1.0.0 (project wins)
```

Remote entries are filtered by `GENICUI_REGISTRY_ALLOWLIST`. The default allow-list is `@genicul-primevue/registry` only. Entries outside the allow-list are dropped with a log warning — they never enter the effective registry.

::callout{type="info"}
The Phase 2 release adds 

`GENICUI_REGISTRY_ALLOWLIST`

 as an enforced env var. The MVP ships the loader and the resolution order; enforcement is gated on the operator setting the env var.
::

## Install flow

::steps
### Install the npm package

```bash
bun add @genicul-primevue/registry
```

The package's `package.json` declares `main` (or `exports`) pointing to its compiled entry. No global registration is needed — the package is just code.

### Load at server boot

```ts
// Source: examples/playground/server/index.ts
import { loadRegistry } from '@genicui/server';
import { primevueRegistry } from '@genicul-primevue/registry';

await loadRegistry(primevueRegistry);
```

`loadRegistry()` validates every component's `propsSchema` (rejects open schemas), walks the schema tree for `additionalProperties: false`, and registers events. Failure to load throws — the server refuses to boot.

### Hot reload on `SIGHUP`

Send `SIGHUP` to the running server and it re-loads the registry without dropping open WebSocket connections:

```bash
kill -HUP $(pgrep -f genicui-server)
```

Existing channels stay open; new `find_ui_component` calls see the updated catalog. F37-AC3 enforces this.

### Discover via `find_ui_component`

```json
{ "name": "find_ui_component", "arguments": { "capability": "table", "tags": ["sortable"] } }
```

→ Returns `ui://genicul/primevue/data-table` with the schema, examples, and `whenToUse`.

### Render via `render_component`

```json
{ "name": "render_component", "arguments": { "name": "DataTable", "props": {...} } }
```

→ Returns the `componentId` + channel + live component HTML.
::

## PassThrough API integration (PrimeVue 4)

`Source: .vaahagents/requirements/specs/features/feature-040-primevue-registry.md` (F40). PrimeVue 4 exposes a PassThrough (`pt`) API that lets registries hook into the framework without DOM probing. GenicUI uses it to wire event handlers and props on the underlying PrimeVue components:

```ts
// Source: registries/primevue/src/data-table.ts
import PrimeVueDataTable from 'primevue/datatable';
import { GenicElement } from '@genicui/runtime';

class DataTableElement extends GenicElement {
  private primevue: PrimeVueDataTable;

  connectedCallback() {
    super.connectedCallback();
    this.primevue = new PrimeVueDataTable({
      pt: {
        root: { class: 'genic-data-table' },
        table: { 'aria-label': this.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? 'Data table' },
      },
      onRowSelect: (e) => this.dispatchEvent(
        new CustomEvent('row_selected', { detail: e.data, bubbles: true, composed: true }),
      ),
    });
  }

  onPatch(patches: JsonPatchOp[]) {
    for (const op of patches) {
      const [key, value] = applyOp(this.props, op);
      this.primevue.setProp(key, value);
    }
  }
}

customElements.define('genic-data-table', DataTableElement);
```

The PassThrough object is the contract surface. The runtime never touches PrimeVue's DOM — PrimeVue re-renders itself when its props change.

## The 8-prop `gv-data-table` API

PrimeVue's DataTable ships 30+ props. The GenicUI wrapper reduces the agent-facing API to 8:

| Prop        | Type                      | Purpose                   |
| ----------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| `rows`      | `object[]`                | The data rows.            |
| `columns`   | `{ key, label }[]`        | Column definitions.       |
| `pageSize`  | `number`                  | Items per page.           |
| `page`      | `number`                  | Current page (0-indexed). |
| `sort`      | `{ key, direction }`      | Current sort.             |
| `filters`   | `Record<string, unknown>` | Per-column filters.       |
| `selection` | `string[]`                | Selected row IDs.         |
| `loading`   | `boolean`                 | Show loading state.       |

Events: `row_selected`, `sort_change`, `filter_change`, `page_change`, `selection_change`. The 8-prop API is the agent's only surface — `lazy`, `virtualScroller`, `paginatorTemplate`, etc. are hidden.

## Open-schema rejection at load

Registries with any `additionalProperties: true` schema fail to boot:

```text
[bootstrap] ERROR: Registry validation failed for "@genicul-X/registry":
  components[0].propsSchema.additionalProperties is true (forbidden)

[bootstrap] Refusing to start. Fix the schema or pin a different version.
```

The check is recursive — every nested `object` in `props.properties.*` and `items.*` is walked. A single open schema anywhere in the tree fails the load.

## What's next

- **Build your own** — see [Guides › Custom Registry](https://genicui.vaah.ai/guides/custom-registry) for a step-by-step walkthrough of authoring a registry from scratch.
- **API surface** — see [API Reference › PrimeVue Registry](https://genicui.vaah.ai/api/primevue-registry) for the full `@genicul-primevue/registry` exports and schema details.
- **Schema enforcement** — see [Trust Boundary › `additionalProperties: false`](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/trust-boundary#additionalproperties-false-enforcement) for the rejection rules.
- **Production deployment** — see [Guides › Production](https://genicui.vaah.ai/guides/production) for how `GENICUI_REGISTRY_ALLOWLIST` is enforced at the network edge.


# Development Setup

This guide walks through the local GenicUI inner loop — clone, install, start the playground, attach an MCP-capable client, and confirm a working render. By the end you should have the server running on `localhost:3040`, the playground mounted in a browser, and four MCP tools visible in your client.

::note
If you just want to consume GenicUI from your own app, 

[Getting Started → Quick Start](https://genicui.vaah.ai/getting-started/quick-start)

 is faster — this guide is for 

**contributors**

 working inside the monorepo.
::

## Prerequisites

| Tool                  | Minimum | Verify with                             |
| --------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Bun                   | 1.3.12  | `bun --version`                         |
| Git                   | 2.40+   | `git --version`                         |
| An MCP-capable client | —       | Claude Code, Cursor, or `mcp-inspector` |

::callout{type="info"}
**About ports:**

 the default server port is 

`3040`

 (set in 

`packages/server/src/config.ts`

). If 

`3040`

 is busy, the server picks the next free port and logs it — read the boot banner before connecting.
::

## Clone and install

::steps{level="3"}
#### Clone the repository

```bash
git clone https://github.com/vaah-ai/GenicUI.git
cd genicui
```

#### Install workspace dependencies

```bash
bun install
```

Bun resolves the full workspace (`packages/*`, `registries/*`, `examples/*`) in one pass. A clean install takes 20–40 seconds.

#### Sanity-check the install

```bash
bun pm ls
```

You should see `@genicui/core`, `@genicui/server`, `@genicui/client`, `@genicui/vite-plugin`, `@genicui/agent-bridge`, and `@genicul-primevue/registry` in the tree. No `@nuxt/ui-pro` — the playground uses `@nuxt/ui` v4 MIT.
::

## Start the server

The production launcher is `packages/server/start.sh`. From the repo root:

```bash
bun --filter @genicui/server start
```

You should see a banner like:

```text
@genicui/server listening on http://localhost:3040
MCP endpoint: http://localhost:3040/mcp
WebSocket:    ws://localhost:3040/ws
```

If the port is in use, the server increments to the next free port — check the banner for the actual URL.

## Start the playground

The playground is the canonical demo app from M5-T4. It runs Nuxt 4 + the PrimeVue registry on a different port (default `3000`).

```bash
bun --filter genicui-playground dev
```

Open `http://localhost:3000&#x60; — you'll see a three-zone layout (sidebar + chat + render surface). The chat panel already has an MCP connection to the server above; sending a message like &#x2A;"render a data table of 5 cities"* should produce a `<genic-data-table>` in the right-hand column.

## Connect your own MCP client

The server exposes four MCP tools over Streamable HTTP at `/mcp`. To connect a separate client:

::code-group
```json [Claude Code (.mcp.json)]
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "genicui-dev": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "http://localhost:3040/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer gnc_live_<32-char-key>"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```bash [mcp-inspector]
npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector \
  --url http://localhost:3040/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer gnc_live_<32-char-key>"
```
::

The dev server prints the auto-generated API key on every boot (`GENICUI_API_KEY`). Copy it from the server log — never check a real key into git.

::callout{type="warning"}
**Test keys only.**

 The dev launcher generates 

`gnc_live_<random>`

 keys for convenience — these are still production-shaped, but never use them outside 

`localhost`

. See 

[Production](https://genicui.vaah.ai/guides/production)

 for the rotation policy.
::

## Hot reload

The server runs under Bun's `--hot` flag, which watches `packages/server/src/**` and `registries/**`. Edit any file and the process restarts in place:

```bash
# Edit packages/server/src/mcp/render-component.ts
# Save — Bun restarts the server in ~200ms
# WS clients reconnect automatically (F33 session recovery)
```

For the **client package**, edit any file in `packages/client/src/` and the Vite dev server hot-reloads the playground page without a full reload.

## Run the test suite

A full test pass takes under 60 seconds and is the fastest way to confirm your install is healthy:

```bash
bun test                    # ~150 unit + 20 integration
bun test --coverage         # adds the coverage gate (~90s)
```

See [Testing](https://genicui.vaah.ai/guides/testing) for the full pyramid and per-layer commands.

## Verification

You should now have four observable outcomes:

1. **`curl http://localhost:3040/health` returns `{"status":"ok"}`** — server is up.
2. **The playground at `http://localhost:3000` shows the three-zone layout** — Nuxt is serving.
3. **Your MCP client lists four tools** (`find_ui_component`, `render_component`, `update_component`, `subscribe_to_events`) — Streamable HTTP auth succeeded.
4. **`bun test` exits 0** — the workspace installed cleanly.

If any of these fail, the most common culprit is port contention (`lsof -i :3040`) or a stale API key from a previous server run.

## What's next

- **Production wiring** — see [Production](https://genicui.vaah.ai/guides/production) for the deploy-time checklist (key rotation, CORS allowlist, observability).
- **Testing** — see [Testing](https://genicui.vaah.ai/guides/testing) for the 150/20/3-5 pyramid and coverage targets.
- **Concepts primer** — see [Protocol](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/protocol) for the wire frame envelope, [MCP Tools](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/mcp-tools) for the four-tool surface.
- **Build your own registry** — see [Building a Custom Registry](https://genicui.vaah.ai/guides/custom-registry) when you're ready to author components.


# Production Checklist

This guide is the **deploy-time gate** for GenicUI. It maps the 10-item pre-deploy list from this [production checklist section](https://genicui.vaah.ai/#the-10-item-checklist) to the exact commands that satisfy each one, plus the env-var reference, secrets policy, and observability hooks you need before serving the first production request.

::callout{type="warning"}
**The 10-item checklist is non-negotiable.**

 Every item maps to a security or reliability invariant that the trust boundary relies on. Skipping any one of them silently downgrades the system.
::

## The 10-item checklist

Run through these in order. Each item is a binary pass/fail — there is no partial credit.

::steps{level="3"}
#### Rotate the API key from `gnc_test_*` to a fresh `gnc_live_*`

```bash
openssl rand -hex 16
# paste into GENICUI_API_KEY on the deploy target
wrangler secret put GENICUI_API_KEY  # Cloudflare
# or: set it in your container/PM2/.env.production
```

  :::callout{type="info"}
  **Why `openssl rand -hex 16`?**

   That's 32 hex chars = 128 bits of entropy, matching the 

  `gnc_live_<32>`

   shape the server validates against.
  :::

#### Configure the CORS allowlist

Set `GENICUI_CORS_ORIGINS` to a comma-separated list of HTTPS origins. Never use `*` in production — the WebSocket upgrade requires a matched `Origin` header.

#### Enable WebSocket origin validation

WS upgrade requests are rejected unless `Origin` matches one of the allowlist entries above. This is on by default — verify your reverse proxy forwards `Origin` (Nginx: `proxy_pass_request_headers on;`).

#### Verify the trust boundary's `stripProtoKeys`

Run a smoke call against `/mcp` with a payload containing `__proto__`, `constructor`, or `prototype` keys:

```bash
curl -X POST http://your-host/mcp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GENICUI_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"render_component","arguments":{"name":"data-table","props":{"__proto__":"x"}}}}'
# expect: {"error":{"code":-32003,"message":"props_invalid"}}
```

A `-32003` confirms the trust boundary is enforcing. A successful render means the stripper is misconfigured.

#### Wire observability — logs, metrics, traces

GenicUI emits structured JSON to stdout (12-factor). Pipe to your aggregator:

```yaml
# docker-compose.yml excerpt
logging:
  driver: json-file
  options:
    max-size: "10m"
    max-file: "3"
```

For Prometheus, expose `/metrics` (opt-in via `GENICUI_METRICS_ENABLED=true`). For distributed traces, the OpenTelemetry SDK is initialized when `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` is set.

#### Move secrets out of `.env` files

`.env` belongs in `.gitignore`. Production secrets belong in:

- Cloudflare: `wrangler secret put ...`
- AWS / GCP: the platform's secret manager
- Kubernetes: sealed-secrets or external-secrets-operator

The server reads env vars on boot — it does not care where they came from.

#### Expose the health-check endpoint

```bash
curl https://your-host/health
# {"status":"ok"}
```

Point your load balancer's health probe at this URL. The endpoint is unauthenticated by design — it never returns session state.

#### Configure persistent session storage

The MVP `memory` store loses sessions on restart. For production:

- **Cloudflare Workers:** Durable Objects (default for `wrangler deploy`)
- **Bun self-host:** SQLite or Postgres (`GENICUI_SESSION_STORE=postgres`)
- **Nitro:** the parent app's existing storage

  :::callout{type="warning"}
  **Backups.**

   Durable Objects' SQLite is replicated to the region automatically. Postgres is on you — wire 

  `pg_dump`

   to your backup schedule before going live.
  :::

#### Terminate TLS at the edge

The server speaks plain HTTP/WS behind a TLS terminator. Cloudflare Workers terminate at the edge automatically; for Bun self-host, use Caddy or Nginx with certbot:

```caddyfile
your-host.com {
  reverse_proxy localhost:8080
  encode zstd gzip
}
```

#### Plan for rate limiting (post-MVP)

The MVP ships rate-limit **hooks** but no enforcement. Before exposing a public endpoint, front GenicUI with Cloudflare WAF rules, Nginx `limit_req`, or your API gateway's policy. Per-API-key buckets need the upcoming `rate-limit-hooks` feature (tracked in the roadmap).
::

## Env var reference

| Var                           | Required | Default                     | Notes                                                              |
| ----------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `GENICUI_API_KEY`             | **yes**  | (random in dev)             | `gnc_live_<32>` chars. Generate via `openssl rand -hex 16`.        |
| `GENICUI_SESSION_STORE`       | optional | `memory`                    | One of `memory` (MVP), `durable-object` (CF), `postgres` (Phase 2) |
| `GENICUI_PORT`                | optional | `8080` (Bun) / `3040` (dev) | Bun self-host only                                                 |
| `GENICUI_LOG_LEVEL`           | optional | `info`                      | `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`                                   |
| `GENICUI_HEARTBEAT_MS`        | optional | `30000`                     | WebSocket ping interval                                            |
| `GENICUI_CORS_ORIGINS`        | **prod** | `*` (dev only)              | Comma-separated allowlist                                          |
| `GENICUI_REGISTRY_ALLOWLIST`  | **prod** | (any)                       | Comma-separated `package@version` patterns                         |
| `GENICUI_METRICS_ENABLED`     | optional | `false`                     | Expose `/metrics`                                                  |
| `GENICUI_REGION`              | optional | (auto)                      | Phase 2; `eu`, `us`, `apac`                                        |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` | optional | (unset)                     | When set, OTel SDK initializes                                     |

## Secrets policy

- **Never commit a real key.** `.env` files are `.gitignore`'d; CI uses `wrangler secret` / repo secrets.
- **Rotate every 90 days minimum** and immediately on any suspected exposure.
- **Scope per environment.** A key leak in staging should not affect production — use separate keys per target.
- **Log scrubbing is built-in.** The structured logger redacts `gnc_live_*` patterns from any log line. Verify with `bun test packages/server/src/auth/__tests__/log-scrub.test.ts`.

## Observability

GenicUI emits one JSON object per line on stdout. Schema:

```json
{"ts":"2026-09-10T12:34:56.789Z","level":"info","channel":"dt-sess9f8e","event":"render_component","duration_ms":12,"componentId":"dt-abc12301HK9X"}
```

| Event              | When                     | Useful for                             |
| ------------------ | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------- |
| `server.hello`     | WS upgrade accepted      | Connection-rate dashboard              |
| `render_component` | Tool call succeeded      | Per-component latency p50/p99          |
| `STATE_DELTA`      | Patch dispatched         | Patch volume / hot-component detection |
| `COMPONENT_EVENT`  | User action crossed wire | Interaction funnel                     |
| `auth.rejected`    | 401 returned             | Brute-force detection                  |

For Prometheus scraping, set `GENICUI_METRICS_ENABLED=true` and point your scraper at `/metrics`. Default metrics: `genicui_render_duration_seconds`, `genicui_ws_connections`, `genicui_patch_apply_total`.

## Verification

Before flipping DNS, run the **production smoke test**:

::steps{level="3"}
#### Render — confirm a component mounts

```bash
curl -X POST https://your-host/mcp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GENICUI_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"render_component","arguments":{"name":"data-table","props":{"rows":[{"id":"1","name":"Alice"}],"columns":[{"key":"name","label":"Name"}]}}}}'
# expect: {"result":{"componentId":"dt-..."}}
```

#### Update — confirm patches dispatch

From a WS client, verify `STATE_DELTA` arrives within 100ms of an `update_component` call.

#### Event — confirm user actions round-trip

Mount an interactive component (e.g. `data-table`), click a row, confirm the agent-side receives `COMPONENT_EVENT` with `payload.detail.rowId`.

#### Health — confirm probes pass

```bash
curl -fsS https://your-host/health
# {"status":"ok"}
```

If all four pass and the 10-item checklist is green, you're production-ready.
::

## What's next

- **Deploy targets** — see [Deployment](https://genicui.vaah.ai/deployment/overview) for Cloudflare Workers, Bun self-host, and Nitro wiring.
- **Trust boundary** — see [Trust Boundary](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/trust-boundary) for the deeper mechanism behind checklist item 4.
- **Registry allowlist** — see [Registries](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/registries) for the trust-tier model and remote-loading rules.
- **API key auth recipe** — see [Cookbook › API Key Authentication](https://genicui.vaah.ai/cookbook/auth) for rotation scripts and per-environment key generation.


# Testing

This guide is the **how we verify** companion to the [testing strategy spec](https://genicui.vaah.ai/guides/testing#the-pyramid). It maps the 150/20/3-5 pyramid onto concrete `bun test` commands, walks the four required `fast-check` property tests, and explains the `@genicui/conformance` runner that every registry must pass before publishing.

## The pyramid

GenicUI follows the classic test pyramid — fast, isolated unit tests form the base; integration tests verify cross-package wiring; a thin e2e layer proves the whole loop in a real browser. Property tests sit beside the unit layer; the conformance suite is the registry-specific spike.

```text
              ╱╲
             ╱  ╲         E2E smoke (3–5 tests)
            ╱    ╲        Full agent turn: render → update → event
           ╱──────╲
          ╱        ╲       Integration tests (~20)
         ╱          ╲      WebSocket frames, MCP tool calls, schema validation
        ╱────────────╲
       ╱              ╲    Unit tests (~150)
      ╱                ╲   SequenceGenerator, JsonPatchEngine, genicSchema, ...
     ╱──────────────────╲
```

| Layer       | Count                     | Speed       | Runs on              |
| ----------- | ------------------------- | ----------- | -------------------- |
| Unit        | \~150                     | <5s total   | Every PR, pre-commit |
| Integration | \~20                      | <30s total  | Every PR             |
| E2E smoke   | 3–5                       | <2min total | Pre-deploy, nightly  |
| Conformance | N×3 (registry × versions) | <60s        | Pre-publish          |

::callout{type="info"}
**Why a thin e2e layer?**

 Unit and integration cover ~93% of bugs. E2E tests are slow and flaky — keep them focused on the 

*happy path that proves the wiring*

 and let the lower layers prove the contracts.
::

## Coverage targets

The lock-in from the [maintainability requirements](https://genicui.vaah.ai/guides/testing#coverage-targets):

| Component         | Line    | Branch |
| ----------------- | ------- | ------ |
| `@genicui/core`   | 80%     | 75%    |
| `@genicui/server` | 80%     | 75%    |
| `@genicui/client` | 70%     | 65%    |
| Tool handlers     | **90%** | 85%    |
| Registry adapters | 60%     | 55%    |
| Framework shims   | 60%     | 55%    |

**Enforcement:** `bun test --coverage` in CI fails the build if any component drops below target. Tool handlers carry the highest target because they are the trust-boundary surface — every tool call passes through them.

## Layer 1 — Unit tests

Pure logic, no I/O. Located next to source as `*.test.ts`.

```bash
bun test packages/*/src
```

Example — `packages/core/src/patch/engine.test.ts`:

```ts
import { describe, it, expect } from 'bun:test';
import fc from 'fast-check';
import { JsonPatchEngine } from './engine';

describe('JsonPatchEngine', () => {
  it('round-trips random pairs (property test)', () => {
    fc.assert(
      fc.property(
        fc.object({ maxDepth: 3 }),
        fc.object({ maxDepth: 3 }),
        (a, b) => {
          const engine = new JsonPatchEngine();
          const patch = engine.diff(a, b);
          return JSON.stringify(engine.apply(patch, a)) === JSON.stringify(b);
        }
      ),
      { numRuns: 10_000 },
    );
  });

  it('returns empty patch for identical objects', () => {
    const engine = new JsonPatchEngine();
    expect(engine.diff({ a: 1 }, { a: 1 })).toEqual([]);
  });
});
```

## Layer 2 — Integration tests

Server + client + transport together. Located in `tests/integration/`. An in-process WS server makes these run in <30s total.

```bash
bun test tests/integration
```

Example — `tests/integration/render-update.test.ts`:

```ts
import { test, expect } from 'bun:test';
import { startTestServer } from '../helpers/server';
import { connectTestClient } from '../helpers/client';

test('agent renders and updates a DataTable', async () => {
  const { server, port } = await startTestServer({ apiKey: 'gnc_live_test' });
  const client = await connectTestClient(`ws://localhost:${port}/ws`, 'gnc_live_test');

  // Render
  const mounted = await client.call('render_component', {
    name: 'data-table',
    props: { rows: [{ id: '1', name: 'Alice' }], columns: [{ key: 'name', label: 'Name' }] },
    surface: 'default',
  });
  expect(mounted.componentId).toMatch(/^dt-[a-f0-9]{8}-[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$/);

  // Wait for COMPONENT_MOUNTED
  const mountedFrame = await client.nextFrame(mounted.componentId);
  expect(mountedFrame.type).toBe('COMPONENT_MOUNTED');

  // Update
  await client.call('update_component', {
    componentId: mounted.componentId,
    patch: [{ op: 'replace', path: '/rows/0/name', value: 'Alicia' }],
  });

  // Verify STATE_DELTA arrives
  const delta = await client.nextFrame(mounted.componentId);
  expect(delta.type).toBe('STATE_DELTA');
  expect(delta.payload).toEqual([{ op: 'replace', path: '/rows/0/name', value: 'Alicia' }]);

  await server.close();
});
```

## Layer 3 — End-to-end smoke

Real browser + real agent. Playwright drives the browser; an MCP inspector drives the agent. Reserved for the full `render → update → event` loop.

```bash
bunx playwright test e2e/full-flow.spec.ts
```

::callout{type="warning"}
**E2E runs pre-deploy, not on every PR.**

 The full Playwright suite takes ~2min; budget it for the deploy pipeline and nightly runs, not the inner loop.
::

## Property tests

For invariants where enumerating cases is impossible, use `fast-check`. GenicUI requires five property tests, each running 10K random cases:

| Feature                | Property                                                                              |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| F3 `SequenceGenerator` | 10K `seq.next()` calls produce monotonic uint64, no duplicates                        |
| F4 `JsonPatchEngine`   | 10K random object pairs satisfy `apply(diff(a, b), a) === b`                          |
| F2 `GenicSchema`       | All TypeBox types round-trip to JSON Schema 2020-12 + back without loss               |
| F14 Trust boundary     | 10K random payloads with `__proto__`, `constructor`, `prototype` all strip those keys |
| F21 Error codes        | 10K random tool calls return codes in `[-32010, -32001]` or the standard MCP range    |

Run them explicitly when iterating on the trust boundary:

```bash
bun test --pattern 'property'
```

## Conformance suite

`@genicui/conformance` is the cross-registry contract — every registry PR must pass before merge.

```ts
// in @genicul-primevue/registry package
import { runConformance } from '@genicui/conformance';
import { registry } from './dist/registry.js';

await runConformance(registry, {
  framework: 'vue3',
  mountPoint: '#test-root',
});
```

The five conformance rules:

1. **Schema valid** — every `propsSchema` parses with `genicSchema()`.
2. **Events declared** — every `composed: true` event has a `detailSchema`.
3. **Lifecycle clean** — `connectedCallback` → render, `disconnectedCallback` → cleanup.
4. **State queries work** — `getState()` returns the same shape as `initialState`.
5. **Wire integration** — render → update → event flow works in a smoke test.

Registry PRs that fail conformance are auto-blocked by `.github/workflows/registry-conformance.yml`.

## Authoring rules

The 6 rules from the testing strategy, restated for grep-ability:

1. **ACs map 1-to-1 to tests.** Each `Given/When/Then` AC gets a test named `<FEATURE>-AC<n>`.
2. **Red-green-refactor.** AC first, failing test second, implementation third.
3. **No network in unit tests.** Stubs for WebSocket, fetch, etc. If you need a network, it belongs in integration or e2e.
4. **Deterministic tests.** All randomness comes from `fast-check`. No `Math.random()`, no `Date.now()` in test bodies — pass timestamps as fixtures.
5. **One assertion per `it()`.** Use `expect()` chains sparingly. If a test has 5+ assertions, split it.
6. **Real references where possible.** Bun's in-process WebSocket is fast enough that mocking is rarely worth the loss of confidence.

## Per-tool test pattern

For each MCP tool, the canonical test layout lives in `packages/server/src/mcp/__tests__/`. The pattern is **one file per tool, four test groups**:

```text
render_component.test.ts
├── AC1: returns valid componentId for valid props
├── AC2: rejects unknown component name (-32004)
├── AC3: rejects payload with __proto__/constructor/prototype (-32003)
└── AC4: emits COMPONENT_MOUNTED on the component's channel
```

The same shape applies to `find_ui_component`, `update_component`, and `subscribe_to_events`. Use `bun test packages/server/src/mcp/__tests__/` to run the full MCP surface.

## CI matrix

| Job                       | Tooling                       | Time budget |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------- | ----------- |
| Lint + format             | ESLint, Prettier              | 30s         |
| Typecheck                 | `tsc --noEmit`                | 60s         |
| Unit + integration        | `bun test`                    | 60s         |
| Coverage gate             | `bun test --coverage`         | 90s         |
| Property tests            | `bun test --pattern property` | 120s        |
| Build                     | `bun run build`               | 60s         |
| E2E smoke (PR only)       | Playwright                    | 180s        |
| Conformance (registry PR) | `bun run test:conformance`    | 60s         |

Total PR CI: \~7 minutes. **Stated budget** — PRs that exceed it get a `perf-budget-exceeded` label.

## Verification

A passing PR needs four observable signals:

```bash
bun test --coverage          # exits 0, all targets met (80/90/60)
bun test --pattern property  # exits 0, 5 property suites green
bun run build                # exits 0
bun run lint                 # exits 0
```

If any one fails, the PR is blocked. Coverage regressions are the most common culprit — bump the target only with an explicit `coverage-justified` label and an updated baseline.

## What's next

- **Concepts primer** — see [Trust Boundary](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/trust-boundary) for the `__proto__` stripper that F14's property test exercises.
- **CI cookbook** — see [Cookbook › Testing Components](https://genicui.vaah.ai/cookbook/testing) for adapter-specific testing patterns and conformance-rule walkthroughs.
- **Build your own registry** — see [Building a Custom Registry](https://genicui.vaah.ai/guides/custom-registry) for the conformance runner's role in the publishing pipeline.


# Building a Custom Registry

This guide walks the five-step process of building a `@genicul-<yourlib>/registry` — the package that turns any component library (PrimeVue, Material, your in-house design system) into a GenicUI surface. The `@genicul-primevue/registry` shipped in M5-T3 is the canonical reference; we'll mirror its layout end-to-end.

::callout{type="info"}
**Why build a registry?**

 Three benefits stack up: (1) typed props with 

`additionalProperties: false`

, (2) 

`PassThrough`

 integration so existing components are wrapped rather than reimplemented, and (3) trust metadata that lets the agent distinguish project-built components from arbitrary npm packages.
::

## The five-step process

::steps{level="3"}
#### Scaffold the package

```bash
mkdir packages/yourlib-registry
cd packages/yourlib-registry
bun init
```

Use the `@genicul-` npm scope (publishing under a different scope is allowed but loses the trust-tier default).

Set up `package.json` with the standard fields — `type: module`, ESM-only, and the `exports` map pointing at `./registry` and `./dist`:

```json
{
  "name": "@genicul-yourlib/registry",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "type": "module",
  "exports": {
    ".": "./dist/index.js",
    "./registry": "./dist/registry.js",
    "./schema": "./dist/schema.js"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "@genicul/core": "workspace:*",
    "@sinclair/typebox": "^0.34.0"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@genicul/conformance": "workspace:*",
    "bun-types": "latest"
  }
}
```

#### Implement `defineRegistry()` with `defineComponent()` for each component

The contract is a single exported `registry` object whose `components` array holds one entry per component. Each entry declares its `propsSchema`, `events`, `tags`, and `examples`. The shape mirrors `ComponentEntry` from `@genicui/server`.

```ts
// src/registry.ts
import { Type } from '@sinclair/typebox';

const ButtonProps = Type.Object({
  label: Type.String(),
  variant: Type.Optional(Type.Union([Type.Literal('primary'), Type.Literal('secondary')])),
  disabled: Type.Optional(Type.Boolean()),
}, { additionalProperties: false });

const ButtonEvents = [
  { name: 'click', payloadSchema: Type.Object({ label: Type.String() }, { additionalProperties: false }) },
];

export const Button = {
  name: 'button',
  version: '1.0.0',
  uri: 'ui://components/button@1.0.0',
  propsSchema: ButtonProps,
  framework: 'yourlib@2.0.0',
  tags: ['button', 'action', 'form'],
  events: ButtonEvents,
  examples: [
    { label: 'Save', variant: 'primary' },
    { label: 'Cancel', variant: 'secondary' },
  ],
};

export const registry = {
  id: '@genicul-yourlib/registry',
  version: '0.1.0',
  framework: 'yourlib',
  components: [Button /*, Input, Card, ... */],
};
```

  :::callout{type="warning"}
  **`additionalProperties: false` is not optional.**

   Every 

  `propsSchema`

   object and every 

  `events[].payloadSchema`

   object must set it. The trust boundary rejects registries that omit it — see 

  [Trust Boundary](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/trust-boundary)

  .
  :::

#### Declare a trust tier in `registry.json`

The trust tier is a runtime config that the server reads at boot. `project` is the safest default — only loaded when the project's own code references it. `user` is for explicitly opted-in packages. `remote` requires the most scrutiny and is gated behind the `GENICUI_REGISTRY_ALLOWLIST` env var.

```json
// registry.json (companion to the JS export)
{
  "id": "@genicul-yourlib/registry",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "framework": "yourlib",
  "trustTier": "project",
  "components": ["button", "input", "card"]
}
```

#### Add per-event `detailSchema` and lifecycle hooks

For every event declared in `events[]`, the component must declare a `payloadSchema` matching the `detail` it dispatches. Components are responsible for emitting events with `composed: true` so they cross the closed Shadow DOM boundary — see [Events](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/events).

```ts
// In your Web Component subclass
this.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('click', {
  detail: { label: this.props.label },
  bubbles: true,
  composed: true,
}));
```

#### Test with `@genicui/conformance`

The conformance runner is a hard gate before publishing:

```ts
// src/registry.test.ts
import { describe, it, expect } from 'bun:test';
import { runConformance } from '@genicui/conformance';
import { registry } from './registry.js';

describe('registry conformance', () => {
  it('passes the 5-rule conformance suite', async () => {
    const result = await runConformance(registry, {
      framework: 'vanilla',
      mountPoint: '#test-root',
    });
    expect(result.failures).toEqual([]);
  });
});
```

CI runs this on every PR that touches `registries/**` — a merge to `main` is blocked until conformance is green.
::

## Walkthrough — `@genicul-primevue/registry`

The shipped PrimeVue registry is the reference implementation. It exports five components — `DataTable`, `InputPair`, `ResultCard`, `CityPicker`, `WeatherCard` — each with a TypeBox schema, an events array, and examples.

```ts
// registries/primevue/src/registry.ts (excerpt)
import { DataTableSchema } from './data-table-schema.js';
import { DataTableEvents } from './data-table-events.js';

export const DataTable = {
  name: 'data-table',
  version: '1.0.0',
  uri: 'ui://components/data-table@1.0.0',
  propsSchema: DataTableSchema,
  framework: 'primevue@4.2.0',
  tags: ['table', 'data', 'grid', 'rows', 'pagination', 'sort', 'filter'],
  events: DataTableEvents,
  examples: [
    {
      rows: [
        { id: '1', name: 'Alice', status: 'active' },
        { id: '2', name: 'Bob', status: 'inactive' },
      ],
      columns: [
        { key: 'name', label: 'Name', sortable: true },
        { key: 'status', label: 'Status', sortable: true, filterable: true },
      ],
      pageSize: 10,
      page: 0,
    },
  ],
};

export const registry = {
  id: '@genicul-primevue/registry',
  version: '0.2.0',
  framework: 'primevue',
  components: [DataTable, InputPair, ResultCard, CityPicker, WeatherCard],
};
```

Two patterns to lift directly:

1. **Schema modules separate from registry.** `data-table-schema.ts`, `data-table-events.ts` live next to the entry — easy to find and conformance-walk in isolation.
2. **Examples carry default values.** The agent uses `examples[]` to seed props when the user request is ambiguous. Two example rows in the PrimeVue registry are why `find_ui_component&#x60; returns it for a bare &#x2A;"show a table"* prompt.

## Publishing

```bash
# 1. Verify the workspace builds
bun --filter @genicul-yourlib/registry build

# 2. Run conformance locally
bun --filter @genicul-yourlib/registry test

# 3. Bump and publish
bun pm version 0.1.0
bun publish --access public
```

Publishing to npm with the `@genicul-` scope gives you the default trust-tier treatment. Private registries (GitHub Packages, Verdaccio) work the same way — set `registry=` in `.npmrc` and the same `bun publish` flow applies.

::callout{type="tip"}
**Versioning for compatibility.**

 Bump the package's minor version when you add a component. Bump the major when you change a 

`propsSchema`

's required keys or remove a component. The trust boundary's schema check is strict — incompatible versions of 

`propsSchema`

 will fail validation at render time.
::

## Verification

Install the freshly published registry into the playground and prove the full round-trip:

```bash
bun add @genicul-yourlib/registry --filter genicui-playground
bun --filter genicui-playground dev
```

Then, from any MCP client:

::steps{level="3"}
#### Mount a component

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3040/mcp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GENICUI_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"render_component","arguments":{"name":"button","props":{"label":"Save","variant":"primary"}}}}'
# expect: {"result":{"componentId":"btn-..."}}
```

#### Trigger the click event from the browser

Open the playground, click the button. The Web Component dispatches `click` with `composed: true`.

#### Receive the event on the agent side

From an MCP-inspector or a subscribed WebSocket client:

```json
{"v":1,"channel":"btn-...","type":"COMPONENT_EVENT","payload":{"action":"click","detail":{"label":"Save"}},"seq":42}
```

If the round-trip works, the registry is correctly wired end-to-end.
::

## What's next

- **Registry contract reference** — see [Registries](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/registries) for the full `defineRegistry` shape and trust-tier semantics.
- **Schema contracts** — see [API Reference › PrimeVue Registry](https://genicui.vaah.ai/api/primevue-registry) for the canonical schema layout your registry will mirror.
- **Trust boundary** — see [Trust Boundary](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/trust-boundary) for why `additionalProperties: false` is mandatory and how the validator strips `__proto__` payloads.
- **Versioning patterns** — see [Cookbook › Registry Versioning](https://genicui.vaah.ai/cookbook/registry-versioning) for migration strategies when a `propsSchema` needs a breaking change.


# Migrating to GenicUI

This guide maps the three most common inbound paths onto GenicUI. For each, we show the wire-level diff, the surface-level diff, and the migration risk. **Migration is the highest-value guide in this section** — it converts evaluators into adopters. Spend the time to walk the path that matches your starting point end-to-end.

::callout{type="info"}
**All three paths keep the agent-side unchanged.**

 The wire protocol GenicUI ships is a superset of AG-UI events; any agent already emitting AG-UI events (which OpenAI Apps SDK, CopilotKit, and the MCP Apps proposal all do) keeps its core loop. You're swapping the 

*surface*

 and the 

*transport hardening*

 — not the reasoning loop.
::

## Inbound overview

| From                | Surface diff                                                                   | Transport diff                                           | Effort |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
| **MCP Apps**        | `resources/list` + `resources/read` → `find_ui_component` + `render_component` | None (Streamable HTTP stays)                             | Small  |
| **OpenAI Apps SDK** | `_meta['openai/outputTemplate']` → GenicUI registry                            | Same `_meta` envelope; GenicUI runs as a runtime adapter | Medium |
| **CopilotKit**      | React custom renderers → GenicElement + closed Shadow DOM                      | AG-UI native already — wire stays                        | Medium |

## From MCP Apps

MCP Apps is the proposal that uses MCP `resources` to vend UI templates. GenicUI replaces the resource layer with its first-class `find_ui_component` + `render_component` tools and keeps everything else.

### Wire-level diff

::tabs
  :::tabs-item{icon="i-lucide-x" label="MCP Apps"}
  ```json
  // Request
  {"method":"resources/list"}
  // Response
  {"resources":[{"uri":"ui://components/data-table","mimeType":"application/json"}]}

  // Render
  {"method":"resources/read","params":{"uri":"ui://components/data-table"}}
  ```
  :::

  :::tabs-item{icon="i-lucide-check" label="GenicUI"}
  ```json
  // Request
  {"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"find_ui_component","arguments":{"query":"data table","topK":1}}}
  // Response
  {"result":{"components":[{"name":"data-table","uri":"ui://components/data-table@1.0.0"}]}}

  // Render
  {"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"render_component","arguments":{"name":"data-table","props":{"rows":[...],"columns":[...]}}}}
  ```
  :::
::

### Migration steps

::steps{level="3"}
#### Replace `resources/list` polling with `find_ui_component`

Search is now query-driven, not enumeration-driven. Drop the polling loop and use the tool inline.

#### Replace `resources/read` with `render_component`

The render path becomes a typed tool call. Validate against the registry's `propsSchema` *before* sending — the server's trust boundary will reject extra keys anyway.

#### Adopt the `ui://components/<name>@<version>` URI grammar

Keep the same `ui://` namespace your clients already expect; just add the `@version` suffix for trust-boundary resolution.

#### Keep your Streamable HTTP transport

GenicUI speaks Streamable HTTP at `/mcp`. Bearer auth stays the same.
::

**Effort:** Small — typically a 1–2 day spike to swap the resource layer. Reference app: `examples/migration-from-mcp-apps/` (planned — see [Verification](https://genicui.vaah.ai/#verification)).

## From OpenAI Apps SDK

OpenAI Apps SDK uses the `_meta['openai/outputTemplate']` envelope to point at HTML templates hosted alongside the MCP server. GenicUI ships a runtime adapter that interprets the same `_meta` keys, so OpenAI consumers keep working unchanged while MCP-native consumers get the full registry.

### Wire-level diff

::tabs
  :::tabs-item{icon="i-lucide-x" label="OpenAI Apps SDK"}
  ```json
  // Tool call with UI hint
  {
    "name":"show_dashboard",
    "_meta":{
      "openai/outputTemplate":"ui://templates/dashboard.html",
      "openai/widgetAccessible":true
    }
  }
  ```

  // Server returns inline HTML via resource
  {"result":{"content": [{"type":"text/html","text":"]

    ::::div
    ...
    ::::

  "}}}
  :::

  :::tabs-item{icon="i-lucide-check" label="GenicUI"}
  ```json
  // Same tool call — _meta is preserved
  {
    "name":"show_dashboard",
    "_meta":{
      "openai/outputTemplate":"ui://components/dashboard@1.0.0",
      "openai/widgetAccessible":true
    }
  }

  // GenicUI resolves the URI to a registry entry and renders via render_component
  {"result":{"componentId":"dash-..."}}
  ```
  :::
::

### Migration steps

::steps{level="3"}
#### Move HTML templates into a GenicUI registry

Each `ui://templates/<name>.html` becomes a component entry in a registry package. The component's render function wraps your existing UI library — no template rewrite needed.

#### Keep the `_meta['openai/...']` envelope untouched

GenicUI's runtime reads it as a hint to apply OpenAI compatibility. OpenAI-side consumers see no change.

#### Add a GenicUI registry entry per template

```ts
const Dashboard = {
  name: 'dashboard',
  version: '1.0.0',
  uri: 'ui://components/dashboard@1.0.0',
  propsSchema: DashboardProps,
  framework: 'openai-template@1',
  tags: ['dashboard', 'analytics'],
  events: [],
  examples: [{ /* default empty state */ }],
};
```

#### Test with both OpenAI consumers and the GenicUI playground

The playground renders every registry entry; OpenAI-side consumers continue to receive `_meta`-shaped responses.
::

**Effort:** Medium — typically 3–5 days for a small template library. The `_meta` envelope preservation is what makes the migration reversible — you can dual-serve during the transition. Reference app: `examples/migration-from-openai/` (planned).

## From CopilotKit

CopilotKit is the AG-UI-native React framework. The wire is already compatible; what changes is the **surface**: React custom renderers become GenicElement + closed Shadow DOM Web Components.

### Wire-level diff

The wire is **identical**. CopilotKit emits AG-UI events; GenicUI consumes them. What changes is the *renderer*:

::tabs
  :::tabs-item{icon="i-lucide-x" label="CopilotKit (React)"}
  ```tsx
  // A CopilotKit custom renderer
  const DataTable: React.FC<{rows: Row[]; columns: Column[]}> = ({ rows, columns }) => (
    <table className="copilotkit-table">
      <thead>{columns.map(c => <th key={c.key}>{c.label}</th>)}</thead>
      <tbody>{rows.map(r => <tr>{columns.map(c => <td>{r[c.key]}</td>)}</tr>)}</tbody>
    </table>
  );
  ```

  // State changes dispatched manually
  useCopilotAction({ name: 'row\_click', handler: ({ rowId }) => emit({ type: 'ROW\_CLICKED', rowId }) });

  ````text

  :::tabs-item{icon="i-lucide-check" label="GenicUI (Web Component)"}
  ```ts
  // A GenicElement subclass — closed Shadow DOM
  class GenicDataTable extends GenicElement {
    static get observedAttributes() { return ['props']; }

    connectedCallback() {
      const { rows, columns } = this.props;
      const shadow = this.attachShadow({ mode: 'closed' });
      shadow.innerHTML = renderTable(rows, columns);
      this.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
        const rowId = (e.target as HTMLElement).dataset.rowId;
        this.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('row_click', {
          detail: { rowId },
          bubbles: true,
          composed: true, // crosses the closed Shadow DOM
        }));
      });
    }
  }
  customElements.define('genic-data-table', GenicDataTable);
  ````

  \:::
  \::

  ### Migration steps

    ::::steps{level="3"}
    #### Port each React renderer to a `GenicElement` subclass

    The `props` attribute replaces `useProps()`; `dispatchEvent` replaces `useCopilotAction()`. Most custom renderers port in a 1:1 mapping.

    #### Replace the React render tree with `<genic-*>` custom elements

    Where the React tree had `<DataTable rows={...} />`, the GenicUI tree has `<genic-data-table props='{"rows":[...]}' />`.

    #### Drop the React wrapper around the agent

    GenicUI runs as a standalone Web Component — no React context provider needed. The agent's runtime (CopilotKit, LangGraph, plain AG-UI) consumes the same wire.

    #### Re-test with the conformance runner

    Each ported component needs to pass `@genicui/conformance` — closed Shadow DOM, `composed: true` events, and the 5-rule smoke.
    ::::

  **Effort:** Medium — typically a week per surface area. The biggest win is removing the React dependency from the runtime; the biggest cost is the learning curve on Web Component lifecycle. Reference app: `examples/migration-from-copilotkit/` (planned).

  ## Decision matrix — when to migrate

  | Symptom                                                                     | Migrate?       | Path                                                                  |
  | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | **Web Components needed** (micro-frontends, embed in non-React apps)        | ✅ Yes          | Any                                                                   |
  | **Multiple UI surfaces** (chat + dashboard + command palette) sharing state | ✅ Yes          | CopilotKit or MCP Apps                                                |
  | **Strict trust boundaries** (security review, sandboxed agents)             | ✅ Yes          | MCP Apps or fresh start                                               |
  | **One-off UI, single agent, no MCP server yet**                             | ❌ Hold         | Stay on OpenAI Apps SDK until you need a second consumer              |
  | **React-only team, no Web Component experience**                            | ⚠️ Pilot first | Try CopilotKit migration on one surface before committing             |
  | **OpenAI-only distribution**                                                | ⚠️ Optional    | The `_meta` adapter runs GenicUI alongside OpenAI; no need to migrate |

    ::::callout{type="tip"}
    **Migrate surface by surface, not all at once.**

     The 

    `_meta`

     adapter and the AG-UI wire compatibility mean GenicUI can run 

    *alongside*

     your existing stack. Pick the lowest-friction surface (typically one component) and prove the round-trip before expanding.
    ::::

  ## Verification

  Each path's **observable outcome** is a working reference app under `examples/`. These are planned and tracked in the migration roadmap:

  - `examples/migration-from-mcp-apps/` — replaces a `resources/list` consumer with `find_ui_component` + `render_component`.
  - `examples/migration-from-openai/` — dual-serves an existing OpenAI Apps SDK server via GenicUI's `_meta` adapter.
  - `examples/migration-from-copilotkit/` — ports a CopilotKit React renderer to a `GenicElement` Web Component.

    ::::callout{type="warning"}
    **Reference apps are not yet shipped.**

     The M5.1-T7 task scope covers the 

    *guide*

    ; the reference apps themselves are scoped for a follow-up milestone (see the 

    [roadmap](https://genicui.vaah.ai/community/roadmap)

    ). Until then, the migration steps above are the source of truth and the conformance suite is the only formal verification gate.
    ::::

  ## What's next

  - **Wire reference** — see [Protocol](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/protocol) for the frame envelope that all three inbound paths eventually resolve to.
  - **Web Component model** — see [Components](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/components) for the closed Shadow DOM lifecycle the CopilotKit migration ports to.
  - **Event flow** — see [Events](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/events) for how `composed: true` events cross from Shadow DOM back to the agent.
  - **First Cookbook recipe** — see [Cookbook › API Key Authentication](https://genicui.vaah.ai/cookbook/auth) for the auth wiring every migration needs end-to-end.
  :::
::


# Core API

The `@genicui/core` package contains the framework-agnostic primitives that every other package depends on. It has no DOM, no Node-specific globals, and no transport — the runtime-agnostic source of truth for schemas, JSON-Patch, sequence generation, and the AG-UI wire envelope.

For the conceptual model behind each export, see [Concepts → Components](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/components) and [Concepts → Frames](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/frames). This page is the reference — terse, table-heavy, verbatim from `packages/core/src/`.

## Constants

### `VERSION`

```ts [packages/core/src/index.ts]
export const VERSION: string = "0.1.0";
```

Package version. Updated automatically by release tooling. The only top-level export that is not re-exported from a submodule.

## Schema builder

A small wrapper around JSON Schema 2020-12 that adds fluent composition, defaults, and a single-call validator. See [Concepts → Components](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/components#schemas) for the rationale.

### `genicSchema(definition)`

```ts [packages/core/src/index.ts]
export { genicSchema, createGenicSchema } from './schema/genic-schema.js';
```

Create a schema from a JSON Schema 2020-12 definition. The returned object bundles the schema, an optional validator, and a helper for merging defaults.

| Parameter    | Type                | Description                                          |
| ------------ | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `definition` | `JSONSchema2020_12` | A JSON Schema 2020-12 document describing the shape. |

**Returns:** `GenicSchemaResult` — `{ schema, validate, defaults }`.

**Example**

```ts
import { genicSchema } from '@genicui/core';

const UserSchema = genicSchema({
  type: 'object',
  required: ['id', 'email'],
  properties: {
    id: { type: 'string' },
    email: { type: 'string', format: 'email' },
    age: { type: 'integer', minimum: 0, default: 18 },
  },
  additionalProperties: false,
});

UserSchema.validate({ id: '1', email: 'a@b.c', age: 30 }); // ok
UserSchema.validate({ id: '1', email: 'a@b.c' });          // ok (default age applied)
UserSchema.validate({ id: '1' });                           // { valid: false, errors: ['/email: required'] }
```

### `createGenicSchema(builder)`

```ts [packages/core/src/index.ts]
export { genicSchema, createGenicSchema } from './schema/genic-schema.js';
```

Fluent builder variant. Useful when the schema shape is computed at runtime.

| Parameter | Type                 | Description                                                                                  |
| --------- | -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `builder` | `GenicSchemaBuilder` | A builder closure that calls `.field()`, `.required()`, `.additionalProperties(false)`, etc. |

**Returns:** `GenicSchemaResult`.

**Example**

```ts
import { createGenicSchema } from '@genicui/core';

const OrderSchema = createGenicSchema((b) =>
  b
    .field('id', { type: 'string' })
    .field('total', { type: 'number', minimum: 0 })
    .required(['id', 'total'])
    .additionalProperties(false),
);
```

### Types — `GenicSchemaOptions`, `GenicSchemaResult`, `GenicSchemaBuilder`, `JSONSchema2020_12`

```ts [packages/core/src/index.ts]
export type {
  GenicSchemaOptions,
  GenicSchemaResult,
  GenicSchemaBuilder,
  JSONSchema2020_12,
} from './schema/types.js';
```

| Type                 | Shape                                                                                                      |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GenicSchemaOptions` | Optional validator / defaults configuration.                                                               |
| `GenicSchemaResult`  | `{ schema: JSONSchema2020_12; validate(input): { valid, errors[] }; defaults?: Record<string, unknown> }`. |
| `GenicSchemaBuilder` | Fluent builder interface.                                                                                  |
| `JSONSchema2020_12`  | Re-export of the JSON Schema 2020-12 root type.                                                            |

## Protocol — AG-UI frame envelope

Single-line JSON envelope used by every WebSocket frame. See [Concepts → Frames](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/frames) for the wire model.

### `SequenceGenerator`

```ts [packages/core/src/index.ts]
export { SequenceGenerator } from './protocol/index.js';
```

Monotonic uint64 sequence number generator. A single instance is shared per WebSocket transport. Each call to `.next()` returns the next number and advances the counter.

```ts
import { SequenceGenerator } from '@genicui/core';

const seq = new SequenceGenerator();
seq.next(); // 1
seq.next(); // 2
```

### `envelope(type, payload, channel, options?)`

```ts [packages/core/src/index.ts]
export { envelope } from './protocol/index.js';
```

Build a single-line JSON frame envelope. Validates the payload against the TypeBox schema for `type` and rejects reserved channels before serializing.

| Parameter        | Type                      | Description                                                           |
| ---------------- | ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `type`           | `AGUIEventType`           | One of the 14 AG-UI event types (see `AG_UI_EVENT_TYPES`).            |
| `payload`        | `Record<string, unknown>` | The event payload — validated against the schema for `type`.          |
| `channel`        | `string`                  | Channel name. Must not equal any `RESERVED_CHANNELS` entry.           |
| `options.seq`    | `number | undefined`      | Override the sequence number. Defaults to `SequenceGenerator.next()`. |
| `options.causes` | `string[] | undefined`    | Causality chain — previous frame `seq` values.                        |

**Returns:** `FrameEnvelope`.

**Throws:** `GenicUIError` if `channel` is reserved or `payload` fails schema validation.

**Example**

```ts
import { envelope, SequenceGenerator } from '@genicui/core';

const seq = new SequenceGenerator();

const frame = envelope(
  'STATE_SNAPSHOT',
  { componentId: 'dt-1', state: { rows: [] } },
  'dt-1',
  { seq: seq.next() },
);
// → { v: 1, channel: 'dt-1', type: 'STATE_SNAPSHOT', payload: {...}, seq: 1 }
```

### `validateChannel(channel)`

```ts [packages/core/src/index.ts]
export { validateChannel } from './protocol/index.js';
```

Throw `GenicUIError` if `channel` matches a reserved channel name (`__system__`, `__broadcast__`, …) or exceeds `MAX_CHANNELS_PER_SOCKET` per socket.

```ts
import { validateChannel } from '@genicui/core';

validateChannel('dt-1');           // ok
validateChannel('__system__');     // throws GenicUIError (RESERVED)
```

### `FrameBuffer`

```ts [packages/core/src/index.ts]
export { FrameBuffer } from './protocol/index.js';
```

In-memory ring buffer of recent frames per socket. The runtime writes each frame it sends; the session-recovery layer reads from it on `Last-Event-ID` replay. Default capacity is `MAX_CHANNELS_PER_SOCKET`; older frames are evicted by `seq`.

```ts
import { FrameBuffer } from '@genicui/core';

const buffer = new FrameBuffer({ capacity: 256 });
buffer.push(frame);
buffer.since(lastEventId); // → FrameBufferResult (all frames with seq > lastEventId)
```

### `FrameEnvelopeSchema`

```ts [packages/core/src/index.ts]
export { FrameEnvelopeSchema } from './protocol/index.js';
```

TypeBox schema for the `FrameEnvelope` shape. Use it when validating externally produced frames (e.g., from a test fixture or a custom transport).

```ts
import { FrameEnvelopeSchema } from '@genicui/core';

const result = FrameEnvelopeSchema.Check(JSON.parse(line));
```

### Protocol constants

```ts [packages/core/src/index.ts]
export {
  PROTOCOL_VERSION,
  RESERVED_CHANNELS,
  ERROR_CODE_RESERVED_CHANNEL,
  MAX_CHANNELS_PER_SOCKET,
  AG_UI_EVENT_TYPES,
} from './protocol/index.js';
```

| Constant                      | Type                       | Description                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `PROTOCOL_VERSION`            | `1`                        | Current wire-protocol version. Bump on breaking envelope changes.                                                        |
| `RESERVED_CHANNELS`           | `readonly string[]`        | Channel names that user code may not bind.                                                                               |
| `ERROR_CODE_RESERVED_CHANNEL` | `number`                   | JSON-RPC-style error code returned when a reserved channel is requested.                                                 |
| `MAX_CHANNELS_PER_SOCKET`     | `256`                      | Hard cap on channels per socket.                                                                                         |
| `AG_UI_EVENT_TYPES`           | `readonly AGUIEventType[]` | The 14 supported AG-UI event types. See [Concepts → Frames](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/frames#the-14-event-types). |

### Types — `FrameEnvelope`, `FrameBufferResult`, `AGUIEventType`, `GenicUIError`

```ts [packages/core/src/index.ts]
export type {
  FrameEnvelope,
  FrameBufferResult,
  AGUIEventType,
} from './protocol/index.js';
```

| Type                | Description                                                                         |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `FrameEnvelope`     | `{ v, channel, type, payload, seq, causes? }` — the shape returned by `envelope()`. |
| `FrameBufferResult` | `{ frames: FrameEnvelope[]; truncated: boolean }` — `since()` query result.         |
| `AGUIEventType`     | String literal union over `AG_UI_EVENT_TYPES`.                                      |
| `GenicUIError`      | Error class thrown by protocol helpers (re-exported).                               |

## JSON-Patch engine

Thin, immutable wrapper around [fast-json-patch](https://github.com/Starcounter-JS/JSON-Patch){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}. See [Concepts → Frames](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/frames#state-delta) for the wire use.

### `JsonPatchEngine`

```ts [packages/core/src/index.ts]
export { JsonPatchEngine } from './patch/index.js';
```

Apply and diff RFC 6902 patches. Defaults to `{ mutate: false }` — every operation returns a new object; the input is never mutated.

```ts
import { JsonPatchEngine } from '@genicui/core';

const engine = new JsonPatchEngine();

// Diff
const patch = engine.diff({ a: 1 }, { a: 2 });
// → [{ op: 'replace', path: '/a', value: 2 }]

// Apply
const next = engine.apply(patch, { a: 1 });
// → { a: 2 }   (input unchanged)
```

### `JsonPatchOperation` (type)

```ts [packages/core/src/index.ts]
export type { JsonPatchOperation } from './patch/index.js';
```

The RFC 6902 op union: `'add' | 'remove' | 'replace' | 'move' | 'copy' | 'test'`.

### `NonSerializableError`, `hasNonSerializable`, `findNonSerializableType`

```ts [packages/core/src/index.ts]
export {
  JsonPatchEngine,
  NonSerializableError,
  hasNonSerializable,
  findNonSerializableType,
} from './patch/index.js';
```

Helpers for catching non-serializable values (`undefined`, functions, symbols, circular refs) before they reach the wire. Used internally by `envelope()` and exported for downstream callers.

```ts
import { hasNonSerializable, findNonSerializableType } from '@genicui/core';

hasNonSerializable({ a: 1 });            // false
hasNonSerializable({ a: undefined });     // true
findNonSerializableType({ a: () => 1 }); // 'function'
```

## SessionStore

Interface for session-scoped state, with a default in-memory implementation.

### `InMemoryStore`

```ts [packages/core/src/index.ts]
export { InMemoryStore } from './session/index.js';
```

`Map`-backed implementation of [`SessionStore`](https://genicui.vaah.ai/#sessionstore-interface). Suitable for single-process development; production deployments should swap in a Durable Object–backed implementation.

```ts
import { InMemoryStore } from '@genicui/core';

const sessions = new InMemoryStore<string, { userId: string }>();
sessions.set('sess-1', { userId: 'u-1' });
sessions.get('sess-1');   // { userId: 'u-1' }
sessions.delete('sess-1');
sessions.on('evicted', (id) => console.log('evicted', id));
```

### `SessionStore` interface

```ts [packages/core/src/index.ts]
export type { SessionStore, SessionStoreCallback } from './session/index.js';
```

```ts [packages/core/src/session/index.ts]
interface SessionStore<K, V> {
  get(key: K): V | undefined;
  set(key: K, value: V): void;
  delete(key: K): boolean;
  has(key: K): boolean;
  size(): number;
  on(event: 'evicted', cb: SessionStoreCallback<K>): void;
  off(event: 'evicted', cb: SessionStoreCallback<K>): void;
}

type SessionStoreCallback<K> = (key: K) => void;
```

The interface is intentionally tiny — implementations are free to add TTL, persistence, and replication.

::note
The 

`M5.1-T8`

 task spec also lists 

`genuiSessionStore`

 as an export. That export does not exist in the current 

`packages/core/src/index.ts`

 — only 

`InMemoryStore`

 and the 

`SessionStore`

 interface are exported. Do not import a 

`genuiSessionStore`

 symbol; it does not exist.
::


# Server API

`@genicui/server` exposes a **single TypeScript export** — `createServer()` — and an **MCP tool JSON-RPC surface** that is the *real* API. Documenting only the TS export would mislead you: every consumer of the server talks to the four MCP tools over HTTP, not to `createServer()` directly.

This page covers both surfaces. For the conceptual model behind each tool, see [Concepts → MCP Tools](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/mcp-tools). For the wire envelope, see [Concepts → Frames](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/frames).

## createServer()

```ts [packages/server/src/index.ts]
export function createServer(): import('elysia').Elysia
```

Boot the HTTP + WebSocket server. Returns the configured Elysia app (useful for test harnesses that want to `.handle()` requests without binding a port). When called as the module entry point (`bun packages/server/bin/start.ts` or via `start.sh`), the server binds and listens.

| Behavior             | Reference                                   |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| Default port         | `3040` (override via `GENICUI_PORT`)        |
| Default hostname     | `0.0.0.0` (override via `GENICUI_HOSTNAME`) |
| Health route         | `GET /health` → `{ status: 'ok' }`          |
| WebSocket route      | `GET /ws` (subprotocol + API-key auth)      |
| MCP route            | `POST /mcp` (streamable JSON-RPC)           |
| Authenticated routes | `GET /api/status`, `GET /api/registries`    |
| Registry loading     | `GENICUI_REGISTRIES_DIR` env var (F43)      |
| API-key loading      | `GENICUI_API_KEY` env var (F46)             |

**Example — programmatic boot**

```ts [start.sh equivalent]
import { createServer } from '@genicui/server';

const app = createServer();
// Elysia is now listening on http://0.0.0.0:3040
```

::note
The runtime entry point is 

`packages/server/bin/start.ts`

 (production launcher) or 

`start.sh`

 at the repo root. 

`createServer()`

 is what both call — see the 

[Server boot sequence](https://genicui.vaah.ai/concepts/mcp-tools#the-server-boot-sequence)

 concept page.
::

## MCP tool surface

The four MCP tools share a common request envelope. Every `tools/call` is a JSON-RPC 2.0 message:

```json [tools/call envelope]
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": "1",
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "<tool-name>",
    "arguments": { /* tool-specific */ }
  }
}
```

A successful response carries the tool result under `result.content[0].text`; an error response uses the standard JSON-RPC error envelope with a GenicUI-specific code (see [Error codes](https://genicui.vaah.ai/#error-codes)).

---

### `find_ui_component`

Search the component catalog for UI components matching a query. Used by agents to *discover* what they can render before calling `render_component`.

**Input schema (Zod — MCP surface)**

```ts [packages/server/src/mcp/tool-registry.ts]
const FindUiComponentInputSchema = z.object({
  query: z.string().min(1).max(512),
  topK: z.number().int().min(1).max(100).optional().default(5),
});
```

| Field   | Type                   | Required         | Description                                                 |
| ------- | ---------------------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `query` | `string` (1–512 chars) | yes              | Free-text search query (component name, tags, description). |
| `topK`  | `integer` (1–100)      | no (default `5`) | Maximum results to return.                                  |

**Output shape** (returned as `result.content[0].text` JSON):

```ts [packages/server/src/mcp/catalog.ts]
interface FindResult {
  components: Array<{
    name: string;
    version: string;
    registryId: string;
    description: string;
    whenToUse: string;
    propsSchema: Record<string, unknown>;
    events: string[];
    examples: Array<Record<string, unknown>>;
    score: number;
  }>;
  reason?: 'no_component_matches';
  disambiguation?: string[];
}
```

**Example request**

```json [MCP POST /mcp]
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": "1",
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "find_ui_component",
    "arguments": { "query": "table", "topK": 3 }
  }
}
```

**Example response**

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": "1",
  "result": {
    "content": [
      {
        "type": "text",
        "text": "{\n  \"components\": [\n    {\n      \"name\": \"DataTable\",\n      \"version\": \"0.1.0\",\n      \"registryId\": \"primevue@4.2.0\",\n      \"description\": \"Display tabular data with sorting, pagination, and row selection.\",\n      \"score\": 0.92\n    }\n  ]\n}"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

**Error codes that may be returned** — none from this tool; validation failures on `query` / `topK` are returned as standard JSON-RPC `-32602` invalid params.

---

### `render_component`

Mount a component on the connected client. Returns a `componentId` for subsequent `update_component` and `subscribe_to_events` calls.

**Input schema (Zod — MCP surface)**

```ts [packages/server/src/mcp/tool-registry.ts]
const RenderComponentInputSchema = z.object({
  name: z.string().min(1).max(128),
  props: z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()),
  surface: z.string().optional(),
  idempotencyKey: z.string().optional(),
  parentComponentId: z.string().optional(),
  replaceComponentId: z.string().optional(),
  transition: z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()).optional(),
  render_mode: z.enum(['inline', 'iframe']).optional(),
});
```

| Field                | Type                      | Required | Description                                                                                            |
| -------------------- | ------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `name`               | `string` (1–128 chars)    | yes      | Component name (e.g., `DataTable`). Must not be a catalog URI like `ui://catalog/primevue/data-table`. |
| `props`              | `Record<string, unknown>` | yes      | Component props — validated against the catalog `propsSchema`.                                         |
| `surface`            | `string`                  | no       | Target rendering surface identifier.                                                                   |
| `idempotencyKey`     | `string`                  | no       | Replay safety — same key returns the same `componentId`.                                               |
| `parentComponentId`  | `string`                  | no       | Mount as a child of an existing component.                                                             |
| `replaceComponentId` | `string`                  | no       | Replace the props/state of an already-mounted component.                                               |
| `transition`         | `Record<string, unknown>` | no       | Transition animation configuration.                                                                    |
| `render_mode`        | `'inline' | 'iframe'`     | no       | Render mode.                                                                                           |

**Output shape**

```ts [packages/server/src/mcp/render-handler.ts]
interface RenderResult {
  componentId: string;
  channel: string;
  name: string;
  schema: Record<string, unknown>;
  events: readonly string[];
  initialState: Record<string, unknown>;
}
```

**Example request**

```json [MCP POST /mcp]
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": "2",
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "render_component",
    "arguments": {
      "name": "DataTable",
      "props": {
        "rows": [
          { "id": "1", "name": "Alice" },
          { "id": "2", "name": "Bob" }
        ],
        "columns": [{ "key": "name", "label": "Name" }],
        "pageSize": 10
      },
      "idempotencyKey": "orders-table-q3"
    }
  }
}
```

**Example response**

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": "2",
  "result": {
    "content": [
      {
        "type": "text",
        "text": "{\n  \"componentId\": \"dt-7f3a9b2c-01HXYZABCDEFGHJKMNPQRST\",\n  \"channel\": \"dt-7f3a9b2c-01HXYZABCDEFGHJKMNPQRST\",\n  \"schema\": { \"type\": \"object\", \"additionalProperties\": false, ... },\n  \"events\": [\"row_selected\", \"sort_change\", \"page_change\", \"filter_change\"],\n  \"initialState\": { \"rows\": [...], \"columns\": [...], \"pageSize\": 10 }\n}"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

**Error codes that may be returned**

| Code                          | Meaning                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-32002 invalid_resource_uri` | `name` is a catalog URI (e.g. `ui://catalog/primevue/data-table`). Pass the bare component name instead. |
| `-32001 component_not_found`  | The component name does not match any catalog entry.                                                     |
